title: Constructor Super (eslint)
description:
Requires `super()` calls in constructors of derived classes and disallows `super()` calls in constructors of non-derived classes.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: For Direction (eslint)
description: Disallow `for` loops where the update clause moves the counter in the wrong direction, preventing the loop from reaching its stop condition.

title: Getter Return (eslint)
description: Requires all getters to have a `return` statement.

title: No Async Promise Executor (eslint)
description: Disallow using an async function as a Promise executor.

title: No Caller (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of `arguments.caller` or `arguments.callee`.

title: No Class Assign (eslint)
description:
Disallow reassigning class variables.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Compare Neg Zero (eslint)
description: Disallow comparing against `-0`

title: No Cond Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow assignment operators in conditional expressions.

title: No Const Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow reassigning `const` variables.

title: No Constant Binary Expression (eslint)
description: Disallow expressions where the operation doesn't affect the value.

title: No Constant Condition (eslint)
description: Disallow constant expressions in conditions.

title: No Control Regex (eslint)
description: Disallows control characters and some escape sequences that match control characters in regular expressions.

title: No Debugger (eslint)
description: Checks for usage of the `debugger` statement.

title: No Delete Var (eslint)
description: The purpose of the `delete` operator is to remove a property from an object.

title: No Dupe Class Members (eslint)
description:
Disallow duplicate class members.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Dupe Else If (eslint)
description: Disallow duplicate conditions in if-else-if chains.

title: No Dupe Keys (eslint)
description:
Disallow duplicate keys in object literals.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Duplicate Case (eslint)
description: Disallow duplicate case labels.

title: No Empty Character Class (eslint)
description: Disallow empty character classes in regular expressions.

title: No Empty Pattern (eslint)
description: Disallow empty destructuring patterns.

title: No Empty Static Block (eslint)
description: Disallow empty static blocks.

title: No Eval (eslint)
description: Disallows referencing the `eval` function. This rule is aimed at preventing potentially dangerous, unnecessary, and slow code by disallowing the use of the `eval()` function.

title: No Ex Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow reassigning exceptions in catch clauses.

title: No Extra Boolean Cast (eslint)
description: This rule disallows unnecessary boolean casts.

title: No Func Assign (eslint)
description:
Disallow reassigning `function` declarations.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Global Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow modifications to read-only global variables.

title: No Import Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow assigning to imported bindings.

title: No Invalid Regexp (eslint)
description: Disallow invalid regular expression strings in RegExp constructors.

title: No Irregular Whitespace (eslint)
description: Disallows the use of irregular whitespace characters in the code.

title: No Iterator (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of the `__iterator__` property.

title: No Loss Of Precision (eslint)
description: Disallow precision loss in numeric literals.

title: No Misleading Character Class (eslint)
description:
This rule reports regular expressions which include multiple code point characters in character class syntax. This includes:
- Characters with combining marks (e.g., `Á` where `A` is followed by a combining acute accent)
- Characters with emoji modifiers (e.g., `👶🏻`)
- Pairs of regional indicator symbols (e.g., `🇯🇵`)
- Characters joined by zero-width joiner (ZWJ) (e.g., `👨👩👦`)
- Surrogate pairs without the Unicode flag (e.g., `/^[👍]$/`)

title: No New Native Nonconstructor (eslint)
description:
Disallow `new` operators with global non-constructor functions (`Symbol`, `BigInt`).
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Nonoctal Decimal Escape (eslint)
description: Disallow `\8` and `\9` escape sequences in string literals.

title: No Obj Calls (eslint)
description:
Disallow calling some global objects as functions.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Self Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow assignments where both sides are exactly the same.

title: No Setter Return (eslint)
description:
Setters cannot return values.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Shadow Restricted Names (eslint)
description: Disallows the redefining of global variables such as `undefined`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `eval`, `globalThis` and `arguments`.

title: No Sparse Arrays (eslint)
description: Disallow sparse arrays.

title: No This Before Super (eslint)
description:
Requires calling `super()` before using `this` or `super`.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Unassigned Vars (eslint)
description: Disallow let or var variables that are read but never assigned.

title: No Unreachable (eslint)
description:
Disallow unreachable code after `return`, `throw`, `continue`, and `break` statements.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code if `allowUnreachableCode: false` is configured in the `tsconfig.json`, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Unsafe Finally (eslint)
description: Disallow control flow statements in `finally` blocks.

title: No Unsafe Negation (eslint)
description:
Disallows negating the left operand of relational operators to prevent logical errors caused by misunderstanding operator precedence or accidental use of negation.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Unsafe Optional Chaining (eslint)
description: Disallow use of optional chaining in contexts where the `undefined` value is not allowed.

title: No Unused Expressions (eslint)
description: This rule disallows unused expressions.

title: No Unused Labels (eslint)
description: Disallow unused labels.

title: No Unused Private Class Members (eslint)
description: Disallow unused private class members.

title: No Unused Vars (eslint)
description: Disallows variable declarations, imports, or type declarations that are not used in code.

title: No Useless Backreference (eslint)
description: Disallows backreferences in regular expressions that will always be ignored because the capture group they refer to has not matched and cannot match at the time the backreference is evaluated.

title: No Useless Catch (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary catch clauses.

title: No Useless Escape (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary escape characters.

title: No Useless Rename (eslint)
description: Disallow renaming import, export, and destructured assignments to the same name.

title: No With (eslint)
description: Disallow `with` statements.

title: Require Yield (eslint)
description: This rule generates warnings for generator functions that do not have the yield keyword.

title: Use Isnan (eslint)
description: Disallows checking against `NaN` without using `isNaN()` call.

title: Valid Typeof (eslint)
description: Enforce comparing `typeof` expressions against valid strings.

title: Default (import)
description: If a default import is requested, this rule will report if there is no default export in the imported module.

title: Namespace (import)
description: Enforces names exist at the time they are dereferenced, when imported as a full namespace (i.e. `import * as foo from './foo'; foo.bar();` will report if bar is not exported by `./foo.`). Will report at the import declaration if there are no exported names found. Also, will report for computed references (i.e. `foo["bar"]()`). Reports on assignment to a member of an imported namespace.

title: Expect Expect (jest)
description: This rule triggers when there is no call made to `expect` in a test, ensure that there is at least one `expect` call made in a test.

title: No Conditional Expect (jest)
description: This rule prevents the use of `expect` in conditional blocks, such as `if` and `catch`. This includes using `expect` in callbacks to functions named `catch`, which are assumed to be promises.

title: No Disabled Tests (jest)
description: This rule raises a warning about disabled tests.

title: No Export (jest)
description: Prevents using exports if a file has one or more tests in it.

title: No Focused Tests (jest)
description: This rule reminds you to remove `.only` from your tests by raising a warning whenever you are using the exclusivity feature.

title: No Standalone Expect (jest)
description:
Prevents `expect` statements outside of a `test` or `it` block. An `expect` within a helper function (but outside of a `test` or `it` block) will not trigger this rule.
Statements like `expect.hasAssertions()` will NOT trigger this rule since these calls will execute if they are not in a test block.

title: Prefer Snapshot Hint (jest)
description: Enforces including a hint string with snapshot matchers (toMatchSnapshot and toThrowErrorMatchingSnapshot).

title: Require To Throw Message (jest)
description: This rule triggers a warning if `toThrow()` or `toThrowError()` is used without an error message.

title: Valid Describe Callback (jest)
description:
This rule validates that the second parameter of a `describe()` function is a callback function. This callback function:
- should not be [async](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/async_function)
- should not contain any parameters
- should not contain any `return` statements

title: Valid Expect (jest)
description: Checks that `expect()` is called correctly.

title: Valid Expect In Promise (jest)
description: Ensures that `expect` calls inside promise chains (`.then()`, `.catch()`, `.finally()`) are properly awaited or returned from the test.

title: Valid Title (jest)
description:
Checks that the titles of Jest and Vitest blocks are valid.
Titles must be:
- not empty,
- strings,
- not prefixed with their block name,
- have no leading or trailing spaces.

title: Check Property Names (jsdoc)
description: Ensures that property names in JSDoc are not duplicated on the same block and that nested properties have defined roots.

title: Check Tag Names (jsdoc)
description: Reports invalid block tag names. Additionally checks for tag names that are redundant when using a type checker such as TypeScript.

title: Implements On Classes (jsdoc)

title: No Defaults (jsdoc)
description: This rule reports defaults being used on the relevant portion of `@param` or `@default`. It also optionally reports the presence of the square-bracketed optional arguments at all.

title: Require Property (jsdoc)
description:
Requires that all `@typedef` and `@namespace` tags have `@property` tags when their type is a plain `object`, `Object`, or `PlainObject`.
Note: this rule can be configured via [jsdoc settings](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/config-file-reference.html#settings) option.

title: Require Property Description (jsdoc)
description: Requires that all `@property` tags have descriptions.

title: Require Property Name (jsdoc)

title: Require Property Type (jsdoc)
description: Requires that each `@property` tag has a type value (within curly brackets).

title: Require Yields (jsdoc)
description: Requires that yields are documented. Will also report if multiple `@yields` tags are present.

title: Google Font Display (nextjs)
description: Enforce font-display behavior with Google Fonts.

title: Google Font Preconnect (nextjs)
description: Enforces the presence of `rel="preconnect"` when using Google Fonts via `<link>` tags.

title: Inline Script Id (nextjs)
description: Enforces that all `next/script` components with inline content or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must have an `id` prop.

title: Next Script For Ga (nextjs)
description: Enforces the use of the `next/script` component when implementing Google Analytics in Next.js applications, instead of using regular `<script>` tags.

title: No Assign Module Variable (nextjs)
description: Prevents the assignment or declaration of variables named `module` in Next.js applications.

title: No Async Client Component (nextjs)
description:
Prevents the use of async functions for client components in Next.js applications. This rule checks for any async function that:
- Is marked with "use client" directive
- Has a name starting with an uppercase letter (indicating it's a component)
- Is either exported as default or assigned to a variable

title: No Before Interactive Script Outside Document (nextjs)
description: Prevents the usage of `next/script`'s `beforeInteractive` strategy outside of `pages/_document.js`. This rule ensures that scripts with the `beforeInteractive` loading strategy are only used in the document component where they are most effective.

title: No Css Tags (nextjs)
description: Prevents manual inclusion of stylesheets using `<link>` tags in Next.js applications. This rule checks for `<link>` tags with `rel="stylesheet"` that reference local CSS files.

title: No Document Import In Page (nextjs)
description: Prevent importing `next/document` outside of `pages/_document.js`.

title: No Duplicate Head (nextjs)
description: Prevent duplicate usage of `<Head>` in `pages/_document.js`.

title: No Head Element (nextjs)
description: Prevents the usage of the native `<head>` element inside a Next.js application.

title: No Head Import In Document (nextjs)
description: Prevents the usage of `next/head` inside a Next.js document.

title: No Html Link For Pages (nextjs)
description: Prevents the usage of `<a>` elements to navigate between Next.js pages.

title: No Img Element (nextjs)
description: Prevent the usage of the `` element due to slower [LCP](https://nextjs.org/learn/seo/lcp) and higher bandwidth.

title: No Page Custom Font (nextjs)
description: Prevent page-only custom fonts.

title: No Script Component In Head (nextjs)
description: Prevent usage of `next/script` in `next/head` component.

title: No Styled Jsx In Document (nextjs)
description: Prevent usage of styled-jsx in `pages/_document.js`.

title: No Sync Scripts (nextjs)
description: Prevent the use of synchronous `<script>` tags in Next.js applications. Require any `<script>` tag with a `src` attribute to also have either the `async` or `defer` attribute.

title: No Title In Document Head (nextjs)
description: Prevent usage of `<title>` with `Head` component from `next/document`.

title: No Typos (nextjs)
description: Detects common typos in Next.js data fetching function names.

title: No Unwanted Polyfillio (nextjs)
description: Prevent use of unsafe polyfill.io domains and duplicate polyfills.

title: Bad Array Method On Arguments (oxc)
description: This rule applies when an array method is called on the arguments object itself.

title: Bad Char At Comparison (oxc)
description: This rule warns when a character accessed with `charAt`, `at`, or bracket notation is compared with a string of length greater than 1.

title: Bad Comparison Sequence (oxc)
description: This rule applies when the comparison operator is applied two or more times in a row.

title: Bad Match All Arg (oxc)
description: This rule warns when the `matchAll` method is called with a regular expression that does not have the global flag (g).

title: Bad Min Max Func (oxc)
description: Checks whether the clamp function `Math.min(Math.max(x, y), z)` always evaluates to a constant result because the arguments are in the wrong order.

title: Bad Object Literal Comparison (oxc)
description: Checks for comparisons between object and array literals.

title: Bad Replace All Arg (oxc)
description: This rule warns when the `replaceAll` method is called with a regular expression that does not have the global flag (g).

title: Const Comparisons (oxc)
description:
Checks for redundant or logically impossible comparisons. This includes:
- Ineffective double comparisons against constants.
- Impossible comparisons involving constants.
- Redundant comparisons where both operands are the same (e.g., a < a).

title: Double Comparisons (oxc)
description: This rule checks for double comparisons in logical expressions.

title: Erasing Op (oxc)
description:
Checks for erasing operations, e.g., `x * 0`.
Based on [https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/erasing_op](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/erasing_op)

title: Missing Throw (oxc)
description: Checks whether the `throw` keyword is missing in front of a `new` expression.

title: Number Arg Out Of Range (oxc)
description: Checks whether the radix or precision arguments of number-related functions exceed the limit.

title: Only Used In Recursion (oxc)
description:
Checks for arguments that are only used in recursion with no side-effects.
Inspired by the `only_used_in_recursion` rule in Clippy.

title: Uninvoked Array Callback (oxc)
description: This rule applies when an Array function has a callback argument used for an array with empty slots.

title: No Callback In Promise (promise)
description: Disallows calling a callback function (`cb()`) inside a `Promise.prototype.then()` or `Promise.prototype.catch()`.

title: No New Statics (promise)
description: Disallows calling new on static `Promise` methods.

title: Valid Params (promise)
description:
Enforces the proper number of arguments are passed to Promise functions.
This rule is generally unnecessary if using TypeScript.

title: Error Boundaries (react)
description:
Validates using error boundaries instead of `try`/`catch` around JSX for errors in child components.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/error-boundaries`.

title: Exhaustive Deps (react)
description: Verifies the list of dependencies for Hooks like `useEffect` and similar.

title: Forward Ref Uses Ref (react)
description: Requires that components wrapped with `forwardRef` must have a `ref` parameter. Omitting the `ref` argument is usually a bug, and components not using `ref` don't need to be wrapped by `forwardRef`.

title: Globals (react)
description:
Disallows assigning to or mutating variables declared outside a component or hook during render; side effects must run outside of render.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/globals`.

title: Immutability (react)
description:
Disallows mutating props, state, hook arguments, hook return values, and other values that are immutable by the Rules of React.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/immutability`.

title: Incompatible Library (react)
description:
Warns on usage of library APIs known to be incompatible with memoization (manual or automatic), such as `react-hook-form`'s `watch()`, TanStack Table's `useReactTable()`, and TanStack Virtual's `useVirtualizer()`.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/incompatible-library`.

title: Jsx Key (react)
description: Enforce `key` prop for elements in an array.

title: Jsx No Duplicate Props (react)
description: This rule prevents duplicate props in JSX elements.

title: Jsx No Undef (react)
description:
Disallow undeclared variables in JSX.
Note that this rule is generally unnecessary if you are using TypeScript, as TypeScript will catch undeclared variables for you.

title: Jsx Props No Spread Multi (react)
description: Enforces that any unique expression is only spread once.

title: No Children Prop (react)
description: Checks that children are not passed using a prop.

title: No Danger With Children (react)
description: Disallows DOM elements from using both `children` and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` properties.

title: No Did Mount Set State (react)
description:
Disallows using `setState` in the `componentDidMount` lifecycle method.
This rule is not relevant for function components, and so can potentially be disabled for modern React codebases.

title: No Did Update Set State (react)
description: Disallow usage of `setState` in `componentDidUpdate`.

title: No Direct Mutation State (react)
description:
This rule forbids the direct mutation of `this.state` in React components.
Note that this rule only applies to class components, it does not apply to function components. For modern React codebases, this rule may not be necessary or relevant.

title: No Find Dom Node (react)
description: This rule disallows the use of `findDOMNode`, which was deprecated in 2018 and removed in React 19.

title: No Is Mounted (react)
description: This rule prevents using `isMounted` in class components.

title: No Render Return Value (react)
description: This rule will warn you if you try to use the `ReactDOM.render()` return value.

title: No String Refs (react)
description: This rule prevents using the deprecated behavior of string literals in ref attributes.

title: No This In Sfc (react)
description: Prevents using `this` in stateless functional components.

title: No Unsafe (react)
description: This rule identifies and restricts the use of unsafe React lifecycle methods.

title: No Will Update Set State (react)
description: Disallows using `setState` in the `componentWillUpdate` lifecycle method.

title: Preserve Manual Memoization (react)
description:
Validates that existing manual memoization (`useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo`) is preserved by the React Compiler: the compiler only compiles code whose inferred dependencies match or exceed the manually specified ones.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization`.

title: Purity (react)
description:
Validates that components and hooks are pure by checking that they do not call known-impure functions such as `Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, or `performance.now()` during render.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/purity`.

title: Refs (react)
description:
Validates correct usage of refs: `ref.current` may not be read or written during render, only in event handlers and effects.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/refs`.

title: Set State In Effect (react)
description:
Disallows calling `setState` synchronously inside an effect body.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`.

title: Set State In Render (react)
description:
Disallows unconditionally setting state during render (including inside `useMemo` callbacks), which triggers additional renders and can cause infinite render loops.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/set-state-in-render`.

title: Static Components (react)
description:
Validates that components are static — defined at module scope rather than recreated on every render — because dynamically recreated components reset state and cause excessive re-rendering.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/static-components`.

title: Use Memo (react)
description:
Validates usage of the `useMemo()` hook against common mistakes, such as passing an async or generator callback or misusing its arguments.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/use-memo`.

title: Void Dom Elements No Children (react)
description:
Disallow void DOM elements (e.g. ``, `
`) from receiving children.

title: Void Use Memo (react)
description:
Validates that `useMemo()` callbacks return a value and that the memoized result is actually used by the component or hook.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/void-use-memo`.

title: Await Thenable (typescript)
description: This rule disallows awaiting a value that is not a Thenable.

title: No Array Delete (typescript)
description: This rule disallows using the delete operator on array values.

title: No Base To String (typescript)
description: This rule requires `toString()` and `toLocaleString()` calls to only be called on objects which provide useful information when stringified.

title: No Duplicate Enum Values (typescript)
description: Disallow duplicate enum member values.

title: No Duplicate Type Constituents (typescript)
description: This rule disallows duplicate constituents of union or intersection types.

title: No Extra Non Null Assertion (typescript)
description: Disallow extra non-null assertions.

title: No Floating Promises (typescript)
description:
This rule disallows "floating" Promises in TypeScript code, which is a Promise that is created without any code to handle its resolution or rejection.
This rule will report Promise-valued statements that are not treated in one of the following ways:
- Calling its `.then()` with two arguments
- Calling its `.catch()` with one argument
- `await`ing it
- `return`ing it
- `void`ing it
This rule also reports when an Array containing Promises is created and not properly handled. The main way to resolv

title: No For In Array (typescript)
description: This rule disallows iterating over an array with a for-in loop.

title: No Implied Eval (typescript)
description: This rule disallows the use of eval-like methods.

title: No Meaningless Void Operator (typescript)
description: This rule disallows the void operator when its argument is already of type void or `undefined`.

title: No Misused New (typescript)
description: Enforces valid definitions of `new` and `constructor`. This rule prevents classes from defining a method named `new`, interfaces from defining a method named `constructor`, and interfaces from defining a construct signature that returns the interface itself.

title: No Misused Spread (typescript)
description: This rule disallows spreading syntax in places where it doesn't make sense or could cause runtime errors.

title: No Non Null Asserted Optional Chain (typescript)
description: Disallow non-null assertions after an optional chain expression.

title: No Redundant Type Constituents (typescript)
description: This rule disallows type constituents of unions and intersections that are redundant.

title: No This Alias (typescript)
description: Disallow aliasing of `this`.

title: No Unnecessary Parameter Property Assignment (typescript)
description: Prevents unnecessary assignment of parameter properties.

title: No Unsafe Declaration Merging (typescript)
description: Disallow unsafe declaration merging.

title: No Unsafe Unary Minus (typescript)
description: This rule disallows using the unary minus operator on a value which is not of type 'number' | 'bigint'.

title: No Useless Default Assignment (typescript)
description: Disallow default assignments that can never be used.

title: No Useless Empty Export (typescript)
description: Disallow empty exports that don't change anything in a module file.

title: No Wrapper Object Types (typescript)
description: Disallow the use of wrapper object types.

title: Prefer As Const (typescript)
description: Enforce the use of `as const` over literal types.

title: Prefer Namespace Keyword (typescript)
description:
This rule reports when the module keyword is used instead of namespace. This rule does not report on the use of TypeScript module declarations to describe external APIs (declare module 'foo' {}).
WARNING
This rule is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
In a future version of TypeScript and Oxlint, this will be a hard error produced by the parser.
See: [https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/54500](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/54500), [https://github.com/

title: Require Array Sort Compare (typescript)
description: This rule requires `Array#sort()` to be called with a comparison function.

title: Restrict Template Expressions (typescript)
description: This rule restricts the types allowed in template literal expressions.

title: Triple Slash Reference (typescript)
description: Disallow certain triple slash directives in favor of ES module import declarations.

title: Unbound Method (typescript)
description: This rule enforces that unbound methods are called with their expected scope.

title: No Await In Promise Methods (unicorn)
description: Disallow using `await` in `Promise` method parameters.

title: No Empty File (unicorn)
description:
Disallows files that do not contain any meaningful code.
This includes files that consist only of:
- Whitespace
- Comments
- Directives (e.g., `"use strict"`)
- Empty statements (`;`)
- Empty blocks (`{}`)
- Hashbangs (`#!/usr/bin/env node`)

title: No Invalid Fetch Options (unicorn)
description: Disallow invalid options in `fetch()` and `new Request()`. Specifically, this rule ensures that a body is not provided when the method is `GET` or `HEAD`, as it will result in a `TypeError`.

title: No Invalid Remove Event Listener (unicorn)
description: It warns when you use a non-function value as the second argument of `removeEventListener`.

title: No New Array (unicorn)
description: Disallow `new Array()`.

title: No Single Promise In Promise Methods (unicorn)
description: Disallow passing single-element arrays to `Promise` methods.

title: No Thenable (unicorn)
description: Disallow defining a `then` property.

title: No Unnecessary Await (unicorn)
description: Disallow awaiting on non-promise values.

title: No Useless Fallback In Spread (unicorn)
description: Disallow useless fallback when spreading in object literals.

title: No Useless Length Check (unicorn)
description:
It checks for an unnecessary array length check in a logical expression.
The cases are:
- `array.length === 0 || array.every(Boolean)` (`array.every` returns `true` if array is has elements)
- `array.length > 0 && array.some(Boolean)` (`array.some` returns `false` if array is empty)

title: No Useless Spread (unicorn)
description:
Disallows using spread syntax in following, unnecessary cases:
- Spread an array literal as elements of an array literal
- Spread an array literal as arguments of a call or a `new` call
- Spread an object literal as properties of an object literal
- Use spread syntax to clone an array created inline

title: Prefer Set Size (unicorn)
description: Prefer `Set#size` over `Set#length` when the `Set` is converted to an array.

title: Prefer String Starts Ends With (unicorn)
description:
Prefer `String#startsWith()` and `String#endsWith()` over using a regex with `/^foo/` or `/foo$/`.
WARNING
This rule is deprecated. Prefer the type-aware `typescript/prefer-string-starts-ends-with` rule instead.

title: Expect Expect (vitest)
description: This rule triggers when there is no call made to `expect` in a test, ensure that there is at least one `expect` call made in a test.

title: Hoisted Apis On Top (vitest)
description: Requires [hoisted](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Hoisting) Vitest APIs (`vi.mock`, `vi.unmock`, and `vi.hoisted`) to appear at the top level of the file.

title: No Conditional Expect (vitest)
description: This rule prevents the use of `expect` in conditional blocks, such as `if` and `catch`. This includes using `expect` in callbacks to functions named `catch`, which are assumed to be promises.

title: No Conditional Tests (vitest)
description: The rule disallows the use of conditional statements within test cases to ensure that tests are deterministic and clearly readable.

title: No Disabled Tests (vitest)
description: This rule raises a warning about disabled tests.

title: No Focused Tests (vitest)
description: This rule reminds you to remove `.only` from your tests by raising a warning whenever you are using the exclusivity feature.

title: No Standalone Expect (vitest)
description:
Prevents `expect` statements outside of a `test` or `it` block. An `expect` within a helper function (but outside of a `test` or `it` block) will not trigger this rule.
Statements like `expect.hasAssertions()` will NOT trigger this rule since these calls will execute if they are not in a test block.

title: Prefer Snapshot Hint (vitest)
description: Enforces including a hint string with snapshot matchers (toMatchSnapshot and toThrowErrorMatchingSnapshot).

title: Require Awaited Expect Poll (vitest)
description: This rule ensures that promises returned by `expect.poll` and `expect.element` calls are handled properly.

title: Require Local Test Context For Concurrent Snapshots (vitest)
description: The rule is intended to ensure that concurrent snapshot tests are executed within a properly configured local test context.

title: Require Mock Type Parameters (vitest)
description:
Enforces the use of type parameters on `vi.fn()`, and optionally on `vi.importActual()` and `vi.importMock()`.
By default, only `vi.fn()` is checked. Set `checkImportFunctions` to `true` to also check `vi.importActual()` and `vi.importMock()`.

title: Require To Throw Message (vitest)
description: This rule triggers a warning if `toThrow()` or `toThrowError()` is used without an error message.

title: Valid Describe Callback (vitest)
description:
This rule validates that the second parameter of a `describe()` function is a callback function. This callback function:
- should not contain any parameters
- should not contain any `return` statements
Vitest supports async `describe()` callbacks, so this rule allows them.

title: Valid Expect (vitest)
description: Checks that `expect()` is called correctly.

title: Valid Expect In Promise (vitest)
description: Ensures that `expect` calls inside promise chains (`.then()`, `.catch()`, `.finally()`) are properly awaited or returned from the test.

title: Valid Title (vitest)
description:
Checks that the titles of Jest and Vitest blocks are valid.
Titles must be:
- not empty,
- strings,
- not prefixed with their block name,
- have no leading or trailing spaces.

title: Warn Todo (vitest)
description: This rule warns about usage of `.todo` in `describe`, `it`, or `test` functions.

title: No Arrow Functions In Watch (vue)
description: This rule disallows using arrow functions when defining a watcher.

title: No Async In Computed Properties (vue)
description: Disallow asynchronous actions in computed properties.

title: No Computed Properties In Data (vue)
description: Disallow accessing computed properties inside `data()`.

title: No Deprecated Data Object Declaration (vue)
description: Disallow object declarations for `data` (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: No Deprecated Delete Set (vue)
description: Disallow using deprecated `$set` / `$delete` (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: No Deprecated Destroyed Lifecycle (vue)
description: Disallow using deprecated `destroyed` and `beforeDestroy` lifecycle hooks in Vue.js 3.0.0+.

title: No Deprecated Events Api (vue)
description: Disallow using deprecated Events API (`$on`, `$off`, `$once`) in Vue.js 3.0.0+.

title: No Deprecated Model Definition (vue)
description: Disallow deprecated `model` definition (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: No Deprecated Props Default This (vue)
description: Disallow deprecated `this` access in props default function (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: No Deprecated Vue Config Keycodes (vue)
description: Disallow using deprecated `Vue.config.keyCodes` (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: No Dupe Keys (vue)
description: Disallow duplication of field names.

title: No Export In Script Setup (vue)
description: Disallow `export` in `<script setup>`

title: No Expose After Await (vue)
description: Disallow asynchronously registered `expose`.

title: No Lifecycle After Await (vue)
description: Disallow asynchronously registered lifecycle hooks.

title: No Reserved Component Names (vue)
description: Disallow Vue component names that collide with HTML / SVG element names (and optionally Vue built-in component names).

title: No Reserved Keys (vue)
description: Disallow overwriting reserved Vue instance keys (e.g. `$data`, `$emit`) or using `_`-prefixed keys inside `data` / `asyncData`.

title: No Reserved Props (vue)
description: Disallow reserved attribute names (e.g. `key`, `ref`) from being used as prop names.

title: No Shared Component Data (vue)
description: Enforce that the `data` property of a Vue component definition is a function.

title: No Side Effects In Computed Properties (vue)
description: Disallow side effects in computed properties.

title: No This In Before Route Enter (vue)
description:
Disallow `this` usage in a `beforeRouteEnter` method.
This rule is only relevant when using `vue-router`.

title: No Watch After Await (vue)
description: Disallow asynchronously-registered `watch`.

title: Prefer Import From Vue (vue)
description: Enforce imports from `vue` instead of `@vue/*`.

title: Require Prop Type Constructor (vue)
description: Require `props` type values to be a constructor function (e.g. `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`) rather than a string, number, or other literal.

title: Require Render Return (vue)
description: Enforce that a `render` function always returns a value.

title: Require Slots As Functions (vue)
description: Enforce properties of `$slots` to be used as functions.

title: Return In Computed Property (vue)
description: Enforce that a `return` statement is present in every computed property.

title: Return In Emits Validator (vue)
description: Enforce that a `return` statement is present in `emits` validators (in Vue.js 3.0.0+).

title: Valid Define Emits (vue)
description:
Enforce valid usage of the `defineEmits` compiler macro in Vue.
This rule reports `defineEmits` compiler macros in the following cases:
- `defineEmits` is referencing locally declared variables.
- `defineEmits` has both a literal type and an argument. e.g. `defineEmits<(e: 'foo')=>void>(['bar'])`
- `defineEmits` has been called multiple times.
- Custom events are defined in both `defineEmits` and `export default {}`.
- Custom events are not defined in either `defineEmits` or `export default {}`.

title: Valid Define Options (vue)
description: Enforce valid use of the `defineOptions` compiler macro.

title: Valid Define Props (vue)
description:
Enforce valid usage of the `defineProps` compiler macro in Vue.
This rule reports `defineProps` compiler macros in the following cases:
- `defineProps` is referencing locally declared variables.
- `defineProps` has both a literal type and an argument. e.g. `defineProps<{ /*props*/ }>({ /*props*/ })`
- `defineProps` has been called multiple times.
- Props are defined in both `defineProps` and `export default {}`.
- Props are not defined in either `defineProps` or `export default {}`.

title: Valid Next Tick (vue)
description: Enforce valid `nextTick` function calls.

title: No Await In Loop (eslint)
description: This rule disallows the use of `await` within loop bodies. (for, for-in, for-of, while, do-while).

title: No Useless Call (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary calls to `.call()` and `.apply()`

title: No Accumulating Spread (oxc)
description: Prevents using object or array spreads on accumulators in `Array.prototype.reduce()` and in loops.

title: No Map Spread (oxc)
description:
Disallow the use of object or array spreads in `Array.prototype.map` and `Array.prototype.flatMap` to add properties/elements to array items.
This rule only seeks to report cases where the spread operator is used to merge objects or arrays, not where it is used to copy them.

title: Jsx No Constructed Context Values (react)
description: Disallows JSX context provider values that cause needless re-renders.

title: No Array Index Key (react)
description: Warn if an element uses an Array index in its key.

title: No Deriving State In Effects (react)
description:
Disallows deriving values from state inside an effect and storing them back into state; derived values should be computed during render instead.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/no-deriving-state-in-effects`.

title: No Object Type As Default Prop (react)
description: Disallows using object, array, function, class, regex, JSX, or `new`-constructed values as default values for destructured React component props.

title: Jsx No Jsx As Prop (react-perf)
description: See the documentation for more details.

title: Jsx No New Array As Prop (react-perf)
description: See the documentation for more details.

title: Jsx No New Function As Prop (react-perf)
description: See the documentation for more details.

title: Jsx No New Object As Prop (react-perf)
description: See the documentation for more details.

title: Prefer Array Find (unicorn)
description: Encourages using `Array.prototype.find` and `Array.prototype.findLast` instead of taking the first or last matching element from `filter(...)`.

title: Prefer Array Flat Map (unicorn)
description: Prefers the use of `.flatMap()` when `map().flat()` are used together.

title: Prefer Set Has (unicorn)
description: Prefer `Set#has()` over `Array#includes()` when checking for existence or non-existence.

title: Class Methods Use This (eslint)
description: Enforce that class methods utilize `this`.

title: Complexity (eslint)
description: Enforces a maximum [cyclomatic complexity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclomatic_complexity) in a program, which is the number of linearly independent paths in a program.

title: Default Case (eslint)
description: Enforces that all `switch` statements include a `default` case, unless explicitly marked with a configured comment.

title: No Alert (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of `alert`, `confirm`, and `prompt`.

title: No Bitwise (eslint)
description: Disallow bitwise operators.

title: No Console (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of console.

title: No Div Regex (eslint)
description: Disallow equal signs explicitly at the beginning of regular expressions.

title: No Empty (eslint)
description: Disallows empty block statements.

title: No Empty Function (eslint)
description: Disallows the usage of empty functions.

title: No Eq Null (eslint)
description: Disallow `null` comparisons without type-checking operators.

title: No Implicit Globals (eslint)
description: Disallows declarations in the global scope, global variable leaks, and writes or redeclarations of read-only globals.

title: No Param Reassign (eslint)
description: Disallow reassigning function parameters or, optionally, their properties.

title: No Plusplus (eslint)
description: Disallow the unary operators `++` and `--`.

title: No Proto (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of the `__proto__` property.

title: No Regex Spaces (eslint)
description: Disallow 2+ consecutive spaces in regular expressions.

title: No Restricted Globals (eslint)
description: Specify global variable names that should not be used in your application.

title: No Restricted Imports (eslint)
description: This rule allows you to specify imports that you don’t want to use in your application. It applies to static imports and to dynamic `import()` with a string-literal source; computed sources like `import(bar)` are ignored.

title: No Restricted Properties (eslint)
description: This rule allows you to disallow access to certain properties on certain objects.

title: No Sequences (eslint)
description: Disallows the use of the comma operator.

title: No Undefined (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of `undefined` as an identifier.

title: No Use Before Define (eslint)
description: Disallows using variables before they are defined.

title: No Var (eslint)
description: ECMAScript 2015 allows programmers to create variables with block scope instead of function scope using the `let` and `const` keywords. Block scope is common in many other programming languages and helps programmers avoid mistakes.

title: No Void (eslint)
description: Disallows the use of the `void` operator.

title: Unicode Bom (eslint)
description: Require or disallow Unicode byte order mark (BOM)

title: Extensions (import)
description: Some file resolve algorithms allow you to omit the file extension within the import source path. For example the node resolver (which does not yet support ESM/import) can resolve ./foo/bar to the absolute path /User/someone/foo/bar.js because the .js extension is resolved automatically by default in CJS. Depending on the resolver you can configure more extensions to get resolved automatically. In order to provide a consistent use of file extensions across your code base, this rule can enforce or

title: No Amd (import)
description: Forbids the use of AMD `require` and `define` calls.

title: No Commonjs (import)
description: Forbids the use of CommonJS `require` calls. Also forbids `module.exports` and `exports.*`.

title: No Cycle (import)
description:
Disallow cyclic dependencies. The rule ensures that there is no resolvable path back to this module via its dependencies.
This includes cycles of depth 1 (imported module imports me), up to an effectively infinite value when the `maxDepth` option is not set.

title: No Default Export (import)
description:
Disallow modules from having default exports.
This can help your editor provide better auto-import functionality, as named exports offer more explicit and predictable imports compared to default exports.

title: No Dynamic Require (import)
description: Forbids imports that use an expression for the module argument. This includes dynamically resolved paths in `require` or `import` statements.

title: No Relative Parent Imports (import)
description: Forbids importing modules from parent directories using relative paths.

title: No Webpack Loader Syntax (import)
description: Forbids using Webpack loader syntax directly in import or require statements.

title: Unambiguous (import)
description: Warn if a `module` could be mistakenly parsed as a `script` instead of as a pure [ES module](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#modules-ecmascript-modules).

title: Check Access (jsdoc)
description:
Checks that `@access` tags use one of the following values:
- "package", "private", "protected", "public"
Also reports:
- Mixing of `@access` with `@public`, `@private`, `@protected`, or `@package` on the same doc block.
- Use of multiple instances of `@access` (or the `@public`, etc) on the same doc block.

title: Empty Tags (jsdoc)
description:
Expects the following tags to be empty of any content:
- `@abstract`
- `@async`
- `@generator`
- `@global`
- `@hideconstructor`
- `@ignore`
- `@inner`
- `@instance`
- `@override`
- `@readonly`
- `@inheritDoc`
- `@internal`
- `@overload`
- `@package`
- `@private`
- `@protected`
- `@public`
- `@static`

title: Anchor Ambiguous Text (jsx-a11y)
description: See the documentation for more details.

title: Handle Callback Err (node)
description: This rule expects that when you're using the callback pattern in Node.js you'll handle the error.

title: No New Require (node)
description: Warn about calling `new` on `require`.

title: No Path Concat (node)
description: Disallows string concatenation with `__dirname` and `__filename`.

title: No Process Env (node)
description: Disallows use of `process.env`.

title: No Top Level Await (node)
description: Disallows the use of top-level `await`, including `for await...of` loops and `await using` declarations that are not nested inside a function.

title: Bad Bitwise Operator (oxc)
description: This rule applies when bitwise operators are used where logical operators are expected.

title: No Async Await (oxc)
description:
Disallows the use of `async`/`await`.
This rule should generally not be used in modern JavaScript/TypeScript codebases without good reason.

title: No Barrel File (oxc)
description:
Disallow the use of barrel files where the file contains `export *` statements, and the total number of modules exceeds a threshold.
The default threshold is 100.

title: No Const Enum (oxc)
description: Disallow TypeScript `const enum`

title: No Optional Chaining (oxc)
description: Disallow [optional chaining](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Optional_chaining).

title: No Rest Spread Properties (oxc)
description: Disallow [Object Rest/Spread Properties](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-object-rest-spread#readme).

title: Catch Or Return (promise)
description: Ensure that each time a `then()` is applied to a promise, a `catch()` must be applied as well. Exceptions are made for promises returned from a function.

title: Spec Only (promise)
description: Disallow use of non-standard Promise static methods.

title: Button Has Type (react)
description: Enforces an explicit `type` attribute for all HTML `button` elements.

title: Forbid Component Props (react)
description: This rule prevents passing of props to components. This rule only applies to Components (e.g. `<Foo />`) and not DOM nodes (e.g. `<div />`). By default this rule prevents passing of props that add lots of complexity (`className`, `style`) to Components. The list of forbidden props can be customized with the forbid option.

title: Forbid Dom Props (react)
description: This rule prevents passing of props to elements. This rule only applies to DOM Nodes (e.g. `<div />`) and not Components (e.g. `<Component />`). The list of forbidden props can be customized with the forbid option.

title: Forbid Elements (react)
description: Allows you to configure a list of forbidden elements and to specify their desired replacements.

title: Invariant (react)
description:
Reports internal React Compiler invariant violations. These indicate a bug in the compiler itself, not in your code — consider reporting them to the oxc or React teams.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/invariant`.

title: Jsx Filename Extension (react)
description: Enforces consistent use of the `.jsx` file extension.

title: Jsx No Literals (react)
description: Disallows usage of unwrapped string literals inside JSX, such as text children of a JSX element or string-valued props.

title: No Clone Element (react)
description: Prevents the usage of `React.cloneElement`, which is considered an anti-pattern in React.

title: No Danger (react)
description: This rule prevents the use of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` prop.

title: No Multi Comp (react)
description: Prevents multiple React components from being defined in the same file.

title: No React Children (react)
description: Disallows the usage of `React.Children`, as it is considered a bad practice.

title: No Unknown Property (react)
description: Disallow usage of unknown DOM properties.

title: Only Export Components (react)
description:
Ensures that modules only export React components (and related HMR-safe items) so that Fast Refresh (a.k.a. hot reloading) can safely preserve component state. Concretely, it validates the shape of your module’s exports and common entrypoints (e.g. `createRoot(...).render(<App />)`) to match what integrations like `react-refresh` expect.
This rule is based on the rule from `eslint-plugin-react-refresh`.

title: Prefer Function Component (react)
description: Enforces that React components are written as function components instead of class components.

title: Rule Suppression (react)
description:
Reports ESLint/Oxlint suppressions of React rules (for example `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`) inside a component or hook. The React Compiler skips functions containing such suppressions, since the suppressed violation may make compilation unsafe.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/rule-suppression`.

title: Syntax (react)
description:
Reports invalid JavaScript encountered by React Compiler while analyzing a component or hook, such as reassigning a `const` binding.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/syntax`.

title: Todo (react)
description:
Reports code that React Compiler cannot yet analyze because it uses features the compiler has not implemented. These are skipped optimizations (bail-outs), not rule violations.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/todo`.

title: Unsupported Syntax (react)
description:
Warns on syntax that React Compiler does not plan to support, such as `eval`; components and hooks using it are skipped, not optimized.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/unsupported-syntax`.

title: Explicit Function Return Type (typescript)
description: This rule enforces that functions have an explicit return type annotation.

title: Explicit Member Accessibility (typescript)
description: Require explicit accessibility modifiers on class properties and methods.

title: Explicit Module Boundary Types (typescript)
description: Require explicit return and argument types on exported functions' and classes' public class methods.

title: No Dynamic Delete (typescript)
description: Disallow using the delete operator on computed key expressions.

title: No Empty Object Type (typescript)
description: To avoid confusion around the `{}` type allowing any non-nullish value, this rule bans usage of the `{}` type. That includes interfaces and object type aliases with no fields.

title: No Explicit Any (typescript)
description: Disallows explicit use of the `any` type.

title: No Import Type Side Effects (typescript)
description: Enforce the use of top-level `import type` qualifier when an import only has specifiers with inline type qualifiers.

title: No Invalid Void Type (typescript)
description: Disallow `void` type usage outside return types and configured generic contexts.

title: No Namespace (typescript)
description: Disallow TypeScript namespaces.

title: No Non Null Asserted Nullish Coalescing (typescript)
description: Disallow non-null assertions in the left operand of a nullish coalescing operator.

title: No Non Null Assertion (typescript)
description: Disallow non-null assertions using the `!` postfix operator.

title: No Require Imports (typescript)
description: Forbids the use of CommonJS `require` calls.

title: No Restricted Types (typescript)
description: Disallow certain types from being used.

title: No Var Requires (typescript)
description:
Disallow `require` statements except in import statements.
NOTE: This rule is intentionally missing the `allow` option from the original typescript-eslint rule. This rule is deprecated in the upstream plugin and the `typescript/no-require-imports` rule should be used instead.

title: Non Nullable Type Assertion Style (typescript)
description: This rule prefers a non-null assertion over an explicit type cast for non-nullable types.

title: Prefer Literal Enum Member (typescript)
description: Explicit enum values must only be literal values (string, number, boolean, etc.).

title: Promise Function Async (typescript)
description: This rule requires any function or method that returns a Promise to be marked as async.

title: Use Unknown In Catch Callback Variable (typescript)
description: This rule enforces using `unknown` for catch clause variables instead of `any`.

title: Import Style (unicorn)
description: Enforce specific import styles per module.

title: No Abusive Eslint Disable (unicorn)
description: Disallows `oxlint-disable` or `eslint-disable` comments without specifying rules.

title: No Anonymous Default Export (unicorn)
description: Disallows anonymous functions and classes as default exports.

title: No Array For Each (unicorn)
description: Forbids the use of `Array#forEach` in favor of a for loop.

title: No Array Reduce (unicorn)
description: Disallow `Array#reduce()` and `Array#reduceRight()`.

title: No Document Cookie (unicorn)
description: Disallows direct use of `document.cookie`.

title: No Length As Slice End (unicorn)
description: Disallow using `length` as the end argument of a `slice` call.

title: No Magic Array Flat Depth (unicorn)
description: Disallow magic numbers for `Array.prototype.flat` depth.

title: No Process Exit (unicorn)
description: Disallow all usage of `process.exit()`.

title: No Useless Error Capture Stack Trace (unicorn)
description: Disallows unnecessary `Error.captureStackTrace(…)` in error constructors.

title: Prefer Modern Math Apis (unicorn)
description: Checks for usage of legacy patterns for mathematical operations.

title: Prefer Module (unicorn)
description: Prefer JavaScript modules (ESM) over CommonJS.

title: Prefer Node Protocol (unicorn)
description: Prefer using the `node:` protocol when importing Node.js built-in modules.

title: Prefer Number Properties (unicorn)
description: Disallows use of `parseInt()`, `parseFloat()`, `isNaN()`, `isFinite()`, `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` as global variables.

title: Require Test Timeout (vitest)
description: Requires every test to have a timeout specified, either as a numeric third argument, a `{ timeout }` option, or via `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: ... })`.

title: Max Props (vue)
description: Enforce a maximum number of props defined for a given Vue component.

title: No Import Compiler Macros (vue)
description: Disallow importing Vue compiler macros.

title: No Multiple Slot Args (vue)
description: Disallow passing multiple arguments to scoped slots.

title: Block Scoped Var (eslint)
description: Enforces that variables are both declared and used within the same block scope. This rule prevents accidental use of variables outside their intended block, mimicking C-style block scoping in JavaScript.

title: No Extend Native (eslint)
description: Prevents extending native global objects such as `Object`, `String`, or `Array` with new properties.

title: No Extra Bind (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary calls to `.bind()`.

title: No Implied Eval (eslint)
description: Disallows passing strings to `setTimeout()`, `setInterval()`, and `execScript()`.

title: No New (eslint)
description: Disallow new operators outside of assignments or comparisons.

title: No Shadow (eslint)
description: Disallows variable declarations from shadowing variables declared in the outer scope.

title: No Underscore Dangle (eslint)
description: Disallows dangling underscores in identifiers.

title: No Unexpected Multiline (eslint)
description: In most cases, semicolons are not required in JavaScript in order for code to be parsed and executed as expected. Typically this occurs because semicolons are automatically inserted based on a fixed set of rules. This rule exists to detect those cases where a semicolon is NOT inserted automatically, and may be parsed differently than expected.

title: No Unmodified Loop Condition (eslint)
description: Disallow references in loop conditions that are never modified within the loop.

title: No Unneeded Ternary (eslint)
description: Disallow ternary operators when simpler alternatives exist.

title: No Useless Concat (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary concatenation of literals or template literals.

title: No Useless Constructor (eslint)
description: Disallow constructors that can be safely removed without changing how the class works.

title: Preserve Caught Error (eslint)
description: Enforces that when re-throwing an error in a catch block, the original error is preserved using the 'cause' property.

title: No Absolute Path (import)
description: Forbid the import of modules using absolute paths.

title: No Empty Named Blocks (import)
description: Enforces that named import blocks are not empty.

title: No Named As Default (import)
description: Reports use of an exported name as the locally imported name of a default export. This happens when an imported default export is assigned a name that conflicts with a named export from the same module.

title: No Named As Default Member (import)
description: Reports the use of an exported name (named export) as a property on the default export. This occurs when trying to access a named export through the default export, which is incorrect.

title: No Self Import (import)
description: Forbids a module from importing itself. This can sometimes happen accidentally, especially during refactoring.

title: No Unassigned Import (import)
description: This rule aims to remove modules with side-effects by reporting when a module is imported but not assigned.

title: No Commented Out Tests (jest)
description: This rule raises a warning about commented-out tests. It's similar to the `no-disabled-tests` rule.

title: Approx Constant (oxc)
description: Disallows the use of approximate constants, instead preferring the use of the constants in the `Math` object.

title: Misrefactored Assign Op (oxc)
description:
[https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/misrefactored_assign_op](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/#/misrefactored_assign_op)
Checks for `a op= a op b` or `a op= b op a` patterns.

title: No Async Endpoint Handlers (oxc)
description: Disallows the use of `async` functions as Express endpoint handlers.

title: No This In Exported Function (oxc)
description: Disallows the use of `this` in exported functions.

title: Always Return (promise)
description: Require returning inside each `then()` to create readable and reusable Promise chains. We also allow someone to throw inside a `then()` which is essentially the same as return `Promise.reject()`.

title: No Multiple Resolved (promise)
description: This rule warns of paths that resolve multiple times in executor functions of Promise constructors.

title: No Promise In Callback (promise)
description: Disallows the use of Promises within error-first callback functions.

title: Capitalized Calls (react)
description:
Disallows calling capitalized functions or methods directly during render instead of rendering them with JSX, since capitalized names are reserved for components.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/capitalized-calls`.

title: Exhaustive Effect Dependencies (react)
description:
Validates that effect dependency arrays are exhaustive and contain no extraneous values.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/exhaustive-effect-dependencies`.

title: Hooks (react)
description:
Runs the React Compiler's Rules of Hooks validation: hooks must be called unconditionally, in a consistent order, at the top level of a component or hook, and not be used as first-class values.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/hooks`.
This rule overlaps with `react/rules-of-hooks`; upstream ships it disabled for that reason.

title: Iframe Missing Sandbox (react)
description: Enforce the `sandbox` attribute on `iframe` elements.

title: Jsx No Comment Textnodes (react)
description: This rule prevents comment strings (e.g. beginning with `//` or `/*`) from being accidentally injected as a text node in JSX statements.

title: Jsx No Script Url (react)
description: Disallow usage of `javascript:` URLs.

title: Memo Dependencies (react)
description:
Validates that `useMemo()` and `useCallback()` declare comprehensive dependency lists without extraneous values.
Powered by the React Compiler, which runs once per file and is shared with the other React Compiler rules. Port of `react-hooks/memo-dependencies`.

title: No Namespace (react)
description: Enforce that namespaces are not used in React elements.

title: No Unstable Nested Components (react)
description: Disallows defining React components inside other components.

title: React In Jsx Scope (react)
description:
Enforces that React is imported and in-scope when using JSX syntax.
Note that this rule is not necessary on React 17+ if you are using the new JSX Transform, and you can disable this rule and skip importing `React` in files with JSX syntax.
If your `tsconfig.json` has `jsx` set to `react-jsx` or `react-jsxdev`, you are using the new JSX Transform. For JavaScript projects using Babel, you are using the new JSX Transform if your React preset configuration (in `.babelrc` or `babel.config.js`) has `

title: Style Prop Object (react)
description: Require that the value of the prop `style` be an object or a variable that is an object.

title: Consistent Return (typescript)
description: Enforce consistent return behavior in functions.

title: No Confusing Non Null Assertion (typescript)
description: Disallow non-null assertion in locations that may be confusing.

title: No Extraneous Class (typescript)
description: This rule reports when a class has no non-static members, such as for a class used exclusively as a static namespace. This rule also reports classes that have only a constructor and no fields. Those classes can generally be replaced with a standalone function.

title: No Unnecessary Boolean Literal Compare (typescript)
description: This rule disallows unnecessary equality comparisons with boolean literals.

title: No Unnecessary Template Expression (typescript)
description: Disallows unnecessary template expressions (interpolations) that can be simplified.

title: No Unnecessary Type Arguments (typescript)
description: This rule disallows type arguments that are identical to the default type parameter.

title: No Unnecessary Type Assertion (typescript)
description: This rule disallows type assertions that do not change the type of an expression.

title: No Unnecessary Type Constraint (typescript)
description: Disallow unnecessary constraints on generic types.

title: No Unnecessary Type Conversion (typescript)
description: Disallow unnecessary type conversion expressions.

title: No Unnecessary Type Parameters (typescript)
description: Disallow type parameters that are declared but not meaningfully used.

title: No Unsafe Enum Comparison (typescript)
description: This rule disallows comparing an enum value with a non-enum value.

title: No Unsafe Type Assertion (typescript)
description: Disallows unsafe type assertions that narrow a type.

title: Consistent Function Scoping (unicorn)
description: Disallow functions that are declared in a scope which does not capture any variables from the outer scope.

title: No Accessor Recursion (unicorn)
description: Disallow recursive access to `this` within getters and setters.

title: No Array Fill With Reference Type (unicorn)
description: Disallows using reference values as `Array#fill()` values.

title: No Array Reverse (unicorn)
description: Prefer using `Array#toReversed()` over `Array#reverse()`.

title: No Array Sort (unicorn)
description: Prefer using `Array#toSorted()` over `Array#sort()`.

title: No Confusing Array With (unicorn)
description: Disallows confusing uses of `Array#with()`.

title: No Instanceof Builtins (unicorn)
Prefer Add Event Listener (unicorn)
description:
Enforces the use of `.addEventListener()` and `.removeEventListener()` over their `on`-function counterparts.
For example, `foo.addEventListener('click', handler);` is preferred over `foo.onclick = handler;` for HTML DOM Events.

title: Require Module Specifiers (unicorn)
description: Enforce a non-empty specifier list in `import` and `export` statements.

title: Require Post Message Target Origin (unicorn)
description:
Enforce using the `targetOrigin` argument with `window.postMessage()`.
Note that this rule may have false positives, as it is not capable of detecting all cases correctly without type information. As such, it may not be a good idea to enable in cases where `postMessage()` may be used with `BroadcastChannel` or worker/service worker contexts (for example, `WorkerGlobalScope#postMessage`, where the second argument is a transfer list or options object, not `targetOrigin`).

title: No Commented Out Tests (vitest)
description: This rule raises a warning about commented-out tests. It's similar to the `no-disabled-tests` rule.

title: No Required Prop With Default (vue)
description: Enforce props with default values to be optional.

title: Require Default Export (vue)
description: Require components to be the default export.

title: Accessor Pairs (eslint)
description: Enforces getter/setter pairs in objects and classes.

title: Array Callback Return (eslint)
description: Enforce return statements in callbacks of array methods.

title: Eqeqeq (eslint)
description: Requires the use of the `===` and `!==` operators, disallowing the use of `==` and `!=`.

title: Max Classes Per File (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum number of classes per file.

title: Max Depth (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum depth that blocks can be nested. This rule helps to limit the complexity of nested blocks, improving readability and maintainability by ensuring that code does not become too deeply nested.

title: Max Lines (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum number of lines per file.

title: Max Lines Per Function (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum number of lines of code in a function. This rule ensures that functions do not exceed a specified line count, promoting smaller, more focused functions that are easier to maintain and understand.

title: Max Nested Callbacks (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum depth that callbacks can be nested. This rule helps to limit the complexity of callback nesting, ensuring that callbacks do not become too deeply nested, improving code readability and maintainability.

title: No Array Constructor (eslint)
description: Disallows creating arrays with the `Array` constructor.

title: No Case Declarations (eslint)
description: Disallow lexical declarations in case clauses.

title: No Constructor Return (eslint)
description: Disallow returning a value from a constructor.

title: No Else Return (eslint)
description: Disallow `else` blocks after `return` statements in `if` statements.

title: No Fallthrough (eslint)
description:
Disallow fallthrough of `case` statements
This rule is aimed at eliminating unintentional fallthrough of one case to the other. As such, it flags any fallthrough scenarios that are not marked by a comment.

title: No Inline Comments (eslint)
description: Disallows comments on the same line as code.

title: No Inner Declarations (eslint)
description: Disallow variable or function declarations in nested blocks.

title: No Lonely If (eslint)
description: Disallow `if` statements as the only statement in `else` blocks.

title: No Loop Func (eslint)
description: Disallows function declarations and expressions inside loop statements when they reference variables declared in the outer scope that may change across iterations.

title: No Negated Condition (eslint)
description: Disallow negated conditions.

title: No New Wrappers (eslint)
description: Disallow `new` operators with the `String`, `Number`, and `Boolean` objects.

title: No Object Constructor (eslint)
description: Disallow calls to the Object constructor without an argument.

title: No Promise Executor Return (eslint)
description: Disallow returning values from Promise executor functions.

title: No Prototype Builtins (eslint)
description: Disallow calling some `Object.prototype` methods directly on objects.

title: No Redeclare (eslint)
description: This rule disallows redeclaring variables within the same scope, ensuring that each variable is declared only once. It helps avoid confusion and unintended behavior in code.

title: No Self Compare (eslint)
description: Disallow comparisons where both sides are exactly the same.

title: No Throw Literal (eslint)
description:
Disallows throwing literals or non-Error objects as exceptions.
WARNING
This rule has been deprecated, please instead use [typescript/only-throw-error](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/only-throw-error.html). The typescript rule is more reliable than the Javascript version, as it has less false positive, and can catch more cases.

title: No Useless Return (eslint)
description: Disallows redundant return statements.

title: No Warning Comments (eslint)
description: Disallows warning comments such as TODO, FIXME, XXX in code.

title: Prefer Promise Reject Errors (eslint)
description:
Require using Error objects as Promise rejection reasons.
WARNING
This rule is not as accurate as the type-aware [typescript/prefer-promise-reject-errors](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/rules/typescript/prefer-promise-reject-errors.html) rule. We recommend using the TypeScript rule when type information is available.

title: Radix (eslint)
description: Enforce the consistent use of the radix argument when using `parseInt()`, which specifies what base to use for parsing the number.

title: Require Await (eslint)
description:
Disallow async functions which have no `await` expression.
NOTE
This rule is inferior to the accuracy of the type-aware `typescript/require-await` rule. If using type-aware rules, always prefer that rule over this one.

title: Require Unicode Regexp (eslint)
description: Enforce the use of `u` or `v` flag on regular expressions.

title: Sort Vars (eslint)
description: Enforce sorting of variable declarations within the same block.

title: Symbol Description (eslint)
description: Require symbol descriptions.

title: Max Dependencies (import)
description: Forbid modules to have too many dependencies (`import` statements only).

title: No Conditional In Test (jest)
description: Disallow conditional statements in tests.

title: Require Param (jsdoc)
description: Requires that all function parameters are documented with JSDoc `@param` tags.

title: Require Param Description (jsdoc)
description: Requires that each `@param` tag has a description value.

title: Require Param Name (jsdoc)
description: Requires that all `@param` tags have names.

title: Require Param Type (jsdoc)
description: Requires that each `@param` tag has a type value (within curly brackets).

title: Require Returns (jsdoc)
description: Requires that return statements are documented. Will also report if multiple `@returns` tags are present.

title: Require Returns Description (jsdoc)
description: Requires that the `@returns` tag has a description value. The error will not be reported if the return value is `void `or `undefined` or if it is `Promise<void>` or `Promise<undefined>`.

title: Require Returns Type (jsdoc)
description: Requires that the `@returns` tag has a type value (in curly brackets).

title: Require Throws Type (jsdoc)
description: Requires a type on the `@throws` tag.

title: Require Yields Type (jsdoc)
description: Requires a type on the `@yields` tag.

title: Branches Sharing Code (oxc)
description: Checks if the `if` and `else` blocks contain shared code that can be moved out of the blocks.

title: Checked Requires Onchange Or Readonly (react)
description: This rule enforces `onChange` or `readOnly` attribute for checked property of input elements. It also warns when `checked` and `defaultChecked` properties are used together.

title: Display Name (react)
description: Enforces that React components have a `displayName` property.

title: Jsx No Target Blank (react)
description: This rule aims to prevent user-generated link hrefs and form actions from creating security vulnerabilities by requiring `rel='noreferrer'` for external link hrefs and form actions, and optionally any dynamically generated link hrefs and form actions.

title: Jsx No Useless Fragment (react)
description: Disallow unnecessary fragments.

title: No Unescaped Entities (react)
description: This rule prevents characters that you may have meant as JSX escape characters from being accidentally injected as a text node in JSX statements.

title: Rules Of Hooks (react)
description: Enforces the Rules of Hooks, ensuring that React Hooks are only called in valid contexts and in the correct order.

title: Ban Ts Comment (typescript)
description: This rule lets you set which directive comments you want to allow in your codebase.

title: Ban Types (typescript)
description:
This rule bans specific types and can suggest alternatives. Note that it does not ban the corresponding runtime objects from being used.
WARNING
This rule is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
Prefer these replacement rules:
- `typescript/no-empty-object-type`
- `typescript/no-unsafe-function-type`
- `typescript/no-wrapper-object-types`
- `typescript/no-restricted-types` (for custom type bans) :::

title: No Confusing Void Expression (typescript)
description: This rule forbids using void expressions in confusing locations such as arrow function returns.

title: No Deprecated (typescript)
description: Disallow using code marked as `@deprecated`.

title: No Misused Promises (typescript)
description: This rule forbids providing Promises to logical locations such as if statements in places where the TypeScript compiler allows them but they are not handled properly. These situations can often arise due to a missing `await` keyword or just a misunderstanding of the way async functions are handled/awaited.

title: No Mixed Enums (typescript)
description: This rule disallows enums from having both string and numeric members.

title: No Unsafe Argument (typescript)
description: This rule disallows calling a function with an argument which is typed as `any`.

title: No Unsafe Assignment (typescript)
description: This rule disallows assigning a value with type `any` to variables and properties.

title: No Unsafe Call (typescript)
description: This rule disallows calling a value with type `any`.

title: No Unsafe Function Type (typescript)
description: Disallow using the unsafe built-in Function type.

title: No Unsafe Member Access (typescript)
description: This rule disallows member access on a value with type `any`.

title: No Unsafe Return (typescript)
description: This rule disallows returning a value with type `any` from a function.

title: Only Throw Error (typescript)
description: This rule disallows throwing non-Error values.

title: Prefer Enum Initializers (typescript)
description: Require each enum member value to be explicitly initialized.

title: Prefer Includes (typescript)
description: Enforce using `.includes()` instead of `.indexOf() !== -1` or `/regex/.test()`.

title: Prefer Nullish Coalescing (typescript)
description: Enforce using the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) instead of logical OR (`||`) or conditional expressions when the left operand might be `null` or `undefined`.

title: Prefer Promise Reject Errors (typescript)
description: This rule enforces passing an Error object to `Promise.reject()`.

title: Prefer Readonly Parameter Types (typescript)
