description: Require function and method parameters to use readonly-compatible types.

title: Prefer Ts Expect Error (typescript)
description: Enforce using @ts-expect-error over @ts-ignore.

title: Related Getter Setter Pairs (typescript)
description: This rule enforces that getters and setters for the same property are defined together and have related types.

title: Require Await (typescript)
description: This rule disallows async functions which do not have an await expression.

title: Restrict Plus Operands (typescript)
description: This rule requires both operands of addition to be the same type and be number, string, or any.

title: Return Await (typescript)
description: This rule enforces consistent returning of awaited values from async functions.

title: Strict Boolean Expressions (typescript)
description: Disallow certain types in boolean expressions.

title: Strict Void Return (typescript)
description: Disallow returning non-void values where a `void` return is expected.

title: Switch Exhaustiveness Check (typescript)
description: This rule requires switch statements to be exhaustive when switching on union types.

title: Consistent Assert (unicorn)
description: Enforces consistent usage of the `assert` module.

title: Consistent Empty Array Spread (unicorn)
description: When spreading a ternary in an array, we can use both `[]` and `''` as fallbacks, but it's better to have consistent types in both branches.

title: Escape Case (unicorn)
description: Enforces defining escape sequence values with uppercase characters rather than lowercase ones. This promotes readability by making the escaped value more distinguishable from the identifier.

title: Explicit Length Check (unicorn)
description: Enforce explicitly comparing the `length` or `size` property of a value.

title: New For Builtins (unicorn)
description:
Enforces the use of `new` for the following builtins: `Object`, `Array`, `ArrayBuffer`, `BigInt64Array`, `BigUint64Array`, `DataView`, `Date`, `Error`, `Float16Array`, `Float32Array`, `Float64Array`, `Function`, `Int8Array`, `Int16Array`, `Int32Array`, `Map`, `WeakMap`, `Set`, `WeakSet`, `Promise`, `RegExp`, `Uint8Array`, `Uint16Array`, `Uint32Array`, `Uint8ClampedArray`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Proxy`, `WeakRef`, `FinalizationRegistry`.
Disallows the use of `new` for the following builtins: `Stri

title: No Array Callback Reference (unicorn)
description: Prevents passing a function reference directly to iterator methods.

title: No Hex Escape (unicorn)
description: Enforces a convention of using [Unicode escapes](https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-escapes#unicode) instead of [hexadecimal escapes](https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-escapes#hexadecimal) for consistency and clarity.

title: No Immediate Mutation (unicorn)
description: Disallows mutating a variable immediately after initialization.

title: No Instanceof Array (unicorn)
description: Require `Array.isArray()` instead of `instanceof Array`.

title: No Lonely If (unicorn)
description: Disallow `if` statements as the only statement in `if` blocks without `else`.

title: No Negated Condition (unicorn)
description: Disallow negated conditions.

title: No Negation In Equality Check (unicorn)
description: Disallow negated expressions on the left of (in)equality checks.

title: No New Buffer (unicorn)
description: Disallows the deprecated `new Buffer()` constructor.

title: No Object As Default Parameter (unicorn)
description: Disallow the use of an object literal as a default value for a parameter.

title: No Static Only Class (unicorn)
description: Disallow `class` declarations that exclusively contain `static` members.

title: No This Assignment (unicorn)
description: Disallow assigning `this` to a variable.

title: No Typeof Undefined (unicorn)
description: Disallow `typeof` comparisons with `undefined`.

title: No Unnecessary Array Flat Depth (unicorn)
description: Disallows passing `1` to `Array.prototype.flat`.

title: No Unnecessary Array Splice Count (unicorn)
description: Disallows passing `.length` or `Infinity` as the `deleteCount` or `skipCount` argument of `Array#splice()` or `Array#toSpliced()`.

title: No Unnecessary Slice End (unicorn)
description: Disallows unnecessarily passing a second argument to `slice(...)`, for cases where it would not change the result.

title: No Unreadable Iife (unicorn)
description: This rule disallows IIFEs with a parenthesized arrow function body.

title: No Useless Promise Resolve Reject (unicorn)
description: Disallows returning values wrapped in `Promise.resolve` or `Promise.reject` in an async function or a `Promise#then`/`catch`/`finally` callback.

title: No Useless Switch Case (unicorn)
description: Disallows useless `default` cases in `switch` statements.

title: No Useless Undefined (unicorn)
description:
Prevents usage of `undefined` in cases where it would be useless.
WARNING
This rule can conflict with the default behaviors of the `eslint/array-callback-return` and `eslint/getter-return` rules. For both rules, you can set the `allowImplicit` option to avoid conflicts.

title: Prefer Array Flat (unicorn)
description: Prefers `Array#flat()` over legacy techniques to flatten arrays.

title: Prefer Array Some (unicorn)
description: Prefers using `Array#some()` over `Array#find()`, `Array#findLast()` with comparing to `undefined`, or `Array#findIndex()`, `Array#findLastIndex()` and a non-zero length check on the result of `Array#filter()`

title: Prefer At (unicorn)
description:
Prefer the `Array#at()` and `String#at()` methods for index access.
This rule also discourages using `String#charAt()`.

title: Prefer Blob Reading Methods (unicorn)
description: Recommends using `Blob#text()` and `Blob#arrayBuffer()` over `FileReader#readAsText()` and `FileReader#readAsArrayBuffer()`.

title: Prefer Code Point (unicorn)
description: Prefer usage of `String#codePointAt` over `String#charCodeAt`. Prefer usage of `String.fromCodePoint` over `String.fromCharCode`.

title: Prefer Date Now (unicorn)
description: Prefers use of `Date.now()` over `new Date().getTime()` or `new Date().valueOf()`.

title: Prefer Dom Node Append (unicorn)
description: Enforces the use of, for example, `document.body.append(div);` over `document.body.appendChild(div);` for DOM nodes.

title: Prefer Dom Node Dataset (unicorn)
description: Use `.dataset` on DOM elements over `getAttribute(…)`, `.setAttribute(…)`, `.removeAttribute(…)` and `.hasAttribute(…)`.

title: Prefer Dom Node Remove (unicorn)
description: Prefers the use of `child.remove()` over `parentNode.removeChild(child)`.

title: Prefer Event Target (unicorn)
description:
Prefers `EventTarget` over `EventEmitter`.
This rule reduces the bundle size and makes your code more cross-platform friendly.
See the [differences](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#eventtarget-and-event-api) between `EventEmitter` and `EventTarget`.

title: Prefer Import Meta Properties (unicorn)
description: Prefer `import.meta.{dirname,filename}` over legacy techniques for getting file paths.

title: Prefer Math Min Max (unicorn)
description: Prefers use of `Math.min()` and `Math.max()` instead of ternary expressions when performing simple comparisons.

title: Prefer Math Trunc (unicorn)
description:
Prefers use of `Math.trunc()` instead of bitwise operations for clarity and more reliable results.
It prevents the use of the following bitwise operations:
- `x | 0` (`bitwise OR` with 0)
- `~~x` (two `bitwise NOT`)
- `x >> 0` (`Signed Right Shift` with 0)
- `x << 0` (`Left Shift` with 0)
- `x ^ 0` (`bitwise XOR Shift` with 0)

title: Prefer Native Coercion Functions (unicorn)
description: Prefers built-in functions over custom ones with the same functionality.

title: Prefer Number Coercion (unicorn)
description: Prefer `Number()` over `parseFloat()` and base-10 `parseInt()`.

title: Prefer Prototype Methods (unicorn)
description: This rule prefers borrowing methods from the prototype instead of the instance.

title: Prefer Query Selector (unicorn)
description: Prefer `.querySelector()` over `.getElementById()`. And prefer `.querySelectorAll()` over `.getElementsByClassName()`, `.getElementsByTagName()`, and `.getElementsByName()`.

title: Prefer Regexp Test (unicorn)
description: Prefers `RegExp#test()` over `String#match()` and `String#exec()`.

title: Prefer Single Call (unicorn)
description:
Enforces combining multiple `Array#{push,unshift}()`, `Element#classList.{add,remove}()`, and `importScripts()` into a single call.
Supersedes the deprecated `unicorn/no-array-push-push` rule.

title: Prefer String Replace All (unicorn)
description: Prefers `String#replaceAll()` over `String#replace()` when using a regex with the global flag.

title: Prefer String Slice (unicorn)
description: Prefer `String#slice()` over `String#substr()` and `String#substring()`.

title: Prefer Top Level Await (unicorn)
description: Prefer top-level await over top-level promises and async function calls.

title: Prefer Type Error (unicorn)
description: Enforce throwing a `TypeError` instead of a generic `Error` after a type checking if-statement.

title: Require Number To Fixed Digits Argument (unicorn)
description: Enforce using the digits argument with `Number#toFixed()`.

title: No Conditional In Test (vitest)
description: Disallow conditional statements in tests.

title: Arrow Body Style (eslint)
description:
This rule can enforce or disallow the use of braces around arrow function body. Arrow functions can use either:
- a block body `() => { ... }`
- or a concise body `() => expression` with an implicit return.

title: Capitalized Comments (eslint)
description: Enforces or disallows capitalization of the first letter of a comment.

title: Curly (eslint)
description: This rule enforces the use of curly braces `{}` for all control statements (`if`, `else`, `for`, `while`, `do`, `with`). It ensures that all blocks are enclosed in curly braces to improve code clarity and maintainability.

title: Default Case Last (eslint)
description: Requires the `default` clause in `switch` statements to be the last one.

title: Default Param Last (eslint)
description: Requires default parameters in functions to be the last ones.

title: Func Name Matching (eslint)
description: Requires function expression names to match the variable or property names they are assigned to, or disallows such matches with `"never"`.

title: Func Names (eslint)
description: Require or disallow named function expressions.

title: Func Style (eslint)
description: Enforce the consistent use of either function declarations or expressions assigned to variables.

title: Grouped Accessor Pairs (eslint)
description: Require grouped accessor pairs in object literals and classes.

title: Guard For In (eslint)
description: Require for-in loops to include an if statement.

title: Id Denylist (eslint)
description: Disallow specified identifiers

title: Id Length (eslint)
description: Enforce a minimum and/or maximum identifier length convention by counting the graphemes for a given identifier.

title: Id Match (eslint)
description: Enforces a naming convention for identifiers by requiring each checked name to match a configured regular expression.

title: Init Declarations (eslint)
description: Require or disallow initialization in variable declarations.

title: Logical Assignment Operators (eslint)
description: This rule requires or disallows logical assignment operator shorthand.

title: Max Params (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum number of parameters in function definitions which by default is three.

title: Max Statements (eslint)
description: Enforce a maximum number of statements in a function. This rule ensures that functions do not exceed a specified statements count, promoting smaller, more focused functions that are easier to maintain and understand.

title: New Cap (eslint)
description: This rule requires constructor names to begin with a capital letter.

title: No Continue (eslint)
description: Disallow `continue` statements.

title: No Duplicate Imports (eslint)
description: Disallow duplicate module imports.

title: No Extra Label (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary labels.

title: No Implicit Coercion (eslint)
description: Disallow shorthand type conversions using operators like `!!`, unary `+`, and `"" +`.

title: No Label Var (eslint)
description: Disallow labels that share a name with a variable.

title: No Labels (eslint)
description: Disallow labeled statements.

title: No Lone Blocks (eslint)
description: Disallows unnecessary standalone block statements.

title: No Magic Numbers (eslint)
description: This rule aims to make code more readable and refactoring easier by ensuring that special numbers are declared as constants to make their meaning explicit. The current implementation does not support BigInt numbers inside array indexes.

title: No Multi Assign (eslint)
description: Disallow use of chained assignment expressions.

title: No Multi Str (eslint)
description: Disallow multiline strings.

title: No Nested Ternary (eslint)
description: Disallow nested ternary expressions.

title: No New Func (eslint)
description: Disallow `new` operators with the `Function` object.

title: No Return Assign (eslint)
description: Disallows assignment operators in return statements.

title: No Script Url (eslint)
description: Disallow `javascript:` URLs.

title: No Template Curly In String (eslint)
description: Disallow template literal placeholder syntax in regular strings. This rule ensures that expressions like `${variable}` are only used within template literals, avoiding incorrect usage in regular strings.

title: No Ternary (eslint)
description: Disallow ternary operators.

title: No Useless Computed Key (eslint)
description: Disallow unnecessary computed property keys in objects and classes.

title: Object Shorthand (eslint)
description: Require or disallow method and property shorthand syntax for object literals

title: One Var (eslint)
description: Enforces variables to be declared either together or separately.

title: Operator Assignment (eslint)
description: This rule requires or disallows assignment operator shorthand where possible. It encourages the use of shorthand assignment operators like `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, etc. to make the code more concise and readable.

title: Prefer Arrow Callback (eslint)
description: Requires using arrow functions for callbacks.

title: Prefer Const (eslint)
description: Requires `const` declarations for variables that are never reassigned after their initial declaration.

title: Prefer Destructuring (eslint)
description: Require destructuring from arrays and/or objects.

title: Prefer Exponentiation Operator (eslint)
description: Disallow the use of `Math.pow` in favor of the `**` operator.

title: Prefer Named Capture Group (eslint)
description: Enforces the use of named capture groups in regular expressions.

title: Prefer Numeric Literals (eslint)
description: Disallow `parseInt()` and `Number.parseInt()` in favor of binary, octal, and hexadecimal literals.

title: Prefer Object Has Own (eslint)
description: Disallow use of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call()` and prefer use of `Object.hasOwn()`

title: Prefer Object Spread (eslint)
description: Disallow using `Object.assign` with an object literal as the first argument and prefer the use of object spread instead.

title: Prefer Regex Literals (eslint)
description: Disallow use of the RegExp constructor in favor of regular expression literals.

title: Prefer Rest Params (eslint)
description: Disallows the use of the `arguments` object and instead enforces the use of rest parameters.

title: Prefer Spread (eslint)
description: Require spread operators instead of `.apply()`

title: Prefer Template (eslint)
description: Require template literals instead of string concatenation.

title: Sort Imports (eslint)
description:
This rule checks all import declarations and verifies that all imports are first sorted by the used member syntax and then alphabetically by the first member or alias name.
When declaring multiple imports, a sorted list of import declarations make it easier for developers to read the code and find necessary imports later.

title: Sort Keys (eslint)
description: When declaring multiple properties, sorting property names alphabetically makes it easier to find and/or diff necessary properties at a later time.

title: Vars On Top (eslint)
description: Enforces that all `var` declarations are placed at the top of their containing scope.

title: Yoda (eslint)
description: Require or disallow "Yoda" conditions. This rule aims to enforce consistent style of conditions which compare a variable to a literal value.

title: Consistent Type Specifier Style (import)
description: Enforces or bans the use of inline type-only markers for named imports.

title: Exports Last (import)
description: This rule enforces that all exports are declared at the bottom of the file. This rule will report any export declarations that comes before any non-export statements.

title: First (import)
description: Forbids any non-import statements before imports except directives.

title: Group Exports (import)
description: Reports when named exports are not grouped together in a single export declaration or when multiple assignments to CommonJS module.exports or exports object are present in a single file.

title: Newline After Import (import)
description: Enforces having one or more empty lines after the last top-level import statement or require call.

title: No Anonymous Default Export (import)
description: Reports if a module's default export is unnamed. This includes several types of unnamed data types; literals, object expressions, arrays, anonymous functions, arrow functions, and anonymous class declarations.

title: No Duplicates (import)
description: Reports if a resolved path is imported more than once in the same module. This helps avoid unnecessary duplicate imports and keeps the code clean.

title: No Mutable Exports (import)
description: Forbids the use of mutable exports with var or let.

title: No Named Default (import)
description: Reports use of a default export as a locally named import.

title: No Named Export (import)
description: Prohibit named exports.

title: No Namespace (import)
description: Enforce a convention of not using namespaced (a.k.a. "wildcard" *) imports.

title: No Nodejs Modules (import)
description: Forbid the use of Node.js builtin modules. Can be useful for client-side web projects that do not have access to those modules.

title: Prefer Default Export (import)
description: Checks whether there is a default export.

title: Consistent Test It (jest)
description:
Jest allows you to choose how you want to define your tests, using the `it` or the `test` keywords, with multiple permutations for each:
- it: `it`, `xit`, `fit`, `it.only`, `it.skip`.
- test: `test`, `xtest`, `test.only`, `test.skip`.

title: Max Expects (jest)
description: This rule enforces a maximum number of `expect()` calls in a single test.

title: Max Nested Describe (jest)
description: This rule enforces a maximum depth to nested `describe()` calls.

title: No Alias Methods (jest)
description: Enforces Jest's canonical matcher names instead of aliases.

title: No Confusing Set Timeout (jest)
description: Disallow confusing usages of `jest.setTimeout`.

title: No Deprecated Functions (jest)
description:
Over the years Jest has accrued some debt in the form of functions that have either been renamed for clarity, or replaced with more powerful APIs.
This rule can also autofix a number of these deprecations for you.

title: No Done Callback (jest)
description: This rule checks the function parameter of hooks & tests for use of the done argument, suggesting you return a promise instead.

title: No Duplicate Hooks (jest)
description: Disallows duplicate hooks in describe blocks.

title: No Hooks (jest)
description: Disallows Jest setup and teardown hooks, such as `beforeAll`.

title: No Identical Title (jest)
description: This rule looks at the title of every test and test suite. It will report when two test suites or two test cases at the same level of a test suite have the same title.

title: No Interpolation In Snapshots (jest)
description: Prevents the use of string interpolations in snapshots.

title: No Jasmine Globals (jest)
description: This rule reports on any usage of Jasmine globals, which are not ported to Jest, and suggests alternatives from Jest's own API.

title: No Large Snapshots (jest)
description: Disallow large snapshots.

title: No Mocks Import (jest)
description: This rule reports imports from a path containing a `__mocks__` component.

title: No Restricted Jest Methods (jest)
description: Restrict the use of specific `jest` and `vi` methods.

title: No Restricted Matchers (jest)
description: Ban specific matchers & modifiers from being used, and can suggest alternatives.

title: No Test Prefixes (jest)
description: Require using `.only` and `.skip` over `f` and `x`.

title: No Test Return Statement (jest)
description: Disallow explicitly returning from tests.

title: No Unneeded Async Expect Function (jest)
description: Disallows unnecessary async function wrapper for expected promises.

title: No Untyped Mock Factory (jest)
description: This rule triggers a warning if `mock()` or `doMock()` is used without a generic type parameter or return type.

title: Padding Around After All Blocks (jest)
description: This rule enforces a line of padding before and after 1 or more `afterAll` statements.

title: Padding Around Test Blocks (jest)
description: This rule enforces a line of padding before and after 1 or more `test`/`it` statements.

title: Prefer Called With (jest)
description: Suggest using `toBeCalledWith()` or `toHaveBeenCalledWith()`

title: Prefer Comparison Matcher (jest)
description:
This rule checks for comparisons in tests that could be replaced with one of the following built-in comparison matchers:
- `toBeGreaterThan`
- `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`
- `toBeLessThan`
- `toBeLessThanOrEqual`

title: Prefer Each (jest)
description: This rule enforces using `each` rather than manual loops.

title: Prefer Ending With An Expect (jest)
description: Enforces that test blocks end with an assertion (`expect` or a configured assertion function).

title: Prefer Equality Matcher (jest)
description: Jest has built-in matchers for expecting equality, which allow for more readable tests and error messages if an expectation fails.

title: Prefer Expect Assertions (jest)
description: Enforces that every test has either `expect.assertions(<number>)` or `expect.hasAssertions()` as its first expression.

title: Prefer Expect Resolves (jest)
description: Prefer `await expect(...).resolves` over `expect(await ...)` when testing promises.

title: Prefer Hooks In Order (jest)
description: Ensures that hooks are in the order that they are called in.

title: Prefer Hooks On Top (jest)
description: While hooks can be setup anywhere in a test file, they are always called in a specific order, which means it can be confusing if they're intermixed with test cases.

title: Prefer Importing Jest Globals (jest)
description: Prefer importing Jest globals (`describe`, `test`, `expect`, etc.) from `@jest/globals` rather than relying on ambient globals.

title: Prefer Jest Mocked (jest)
description:
When working with mocks of functions using Jest, it's recommended to use the `jest.mocked()` helper function to properly type the mocked functions. This rule enforces the use of `jest.mocked()` for better type safety and readability.
Restricted types:
- `jest.Mock`
- `jest.MockedFunction`
- `jest.MockedClass`
- `jest.MockedObject`

title: Prefer Lowercase Title (jest)
description: Enforce `it`, `test`, `describe`, and `bench` to have descriptions that begin with a lowercase letter. This provides more readable test failures.

title: Prefer Mock Promise Shorthand (jest)
description: When working with mocks of functions that return promises, Jest provides some API sugar functions to reduce the amount of boilerplate you have to write. These methods should be preferred when possible.

title: Prefer Mock Return Shorthand (jest)
description: When working with mocks of functions that return simple values, Jest provides some API sugar functions to reduce the amount of boilerplate you have to write.

title: Prefer Spy On (jest)
description:
When mocking a function by overwriting a property you have to manually restore the original implementation when cleaning up. When using `jest.spyOn()` Jest keeps track of changes, and they can be restored with `jest.restoreAllMocks()`, `mockFn.mockRestore()` or by setting `restoreMocks` to `true` in the Jest config.

title: Prefer Strict Equal (jest)
description: This rule triggers a warning if `toEqual()` is used to assert equality.

title: Prefer To Be (jest)
description: Recommends using `toBe` matcher for primitive literals and specific matchers for `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN`.

title: Prefer To Contain (jest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toContain()` should be used upon asserting expectations on an array containing an object.

title: Prefer To Have Been Called (jest)
description: Suggests using `toHaveBeenCalled()` or `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` over `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0)` or `toBeCalledTimes(0)`.

title: Prefer To Have Been Called Times (jest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` should be used instead of directly checking the length of `mock.calls`.

title: Prefer To Have Length (jest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toHaveLength()` should be used upon asserting expectations on objects length property.

title: Prefer Todo (jest)
description: When test cases are empty then it is better to mark them as `test.todo` as it will be highlighted in the summary output.

title: Require Hook (jest)
description:
This rule flags any expression that is either at the toplevel of a test file or directly within the body of a `describe`, except for the following:
- `import` statements
- `const` variables
- `let` declarations, and initializations to `null` or `undefined`
- Classes
- Types
- Calls to the standard Jest globals

title: Require Top Level Describe (jest)
description: Requires test cases and hooks to be inside a top-level `describe` block.

title: No Blank Blocks (jsdoc)
description: Reports and optionally removes blocks with whitespace only.

title: Require Throws Description (jsdoc)
description: Requires a description for `@throws` tags.

title: Require Yields Description (jsdoc)
description: Requires a description for `@yields` tags.

title: Callback Return (node)
description: Require `return` statements after callbacks.

title: Exports Style (node)
description: Enforce either `module.exports` or `exports`.

title: Global Require (node)
description: Require `require()` calls to be placed at top-level module scope.

title: No Exports Assign (node)
description: Disallows assignment to `exports`.

title: No Mixed Requires (node)
description: Disallows `require` calls to be mixed with regular variable declarations.

title: No Sync (node)
description: Disallows synchronous methods from being called in Node.js code.

title: Avoid New (promise)
description: Disallow creating promises with `new Promise()`.

title: No Nesting (promise)
description: Disallow nested `then()` or `catch()` statements.

title: No Return Wrap (promise)
description:
Prevents unnecessary wrapping of return values in promises with either `Promise.resolve` or `Promise.reject`.
This rule enforces the following stances:
-
When a promise is to be resolved, instead of returning `Promise.resolve(value)` it is better to return the raw value with `return value` instead.
-
When a promise is to be rejected, instead of returning `Promise.reject(error)`, instead the raw error value should be thrown as in `throw error`.
There is an option to turn off the enforcing of 2, s

title: Param Names (promise)
description: Enforce standard parameter names for Promise constructors.

title: Prefer Await To Callbacks (promise)
description: The rule encourages the use of `async/await` for handling asynchronous code instead of traditional callback functions. `async/await`, introduced in ES2017, provides a clearer and more concise syntax for writing asynchronous code, making it easier to read and maintain.

title: Prefer Await To Then (promise)
description: Prefer `await` to `then()`/`catch()`/`finally()` for reading Promise values.

title: Prefer Catch (promise)
description: Prefer `catch` to `then(a, b)` and `then(null, b)`. This rule disallows the passing of an argument into the second parameter of `then` calls for handling promise errors.

title: Function Component Definition (react)
description: Enforces a consistent function form for React function components.

title: Hook Use State (react)
description: Ensure destructuring and symmetric naming of useState hook value and setter variables.

title: Jsx Boolean Value (react)
description: Enforce a consistent boolean attribute style in your code.

title: Jsx Curly Brace Presence (react)
description:
Disallow unnecessary JSX expressions when literals alone are sufficient or enforce JSX expressions on literals in JSX children or attributes.
This rule allows you to enforce curly braces or disallow unnecessary curly braces in JSX props and/or children.
For situations where JSX expressions are unnecessary, please refer to [the React doc](https://react.dev/learn/writing-markup-with-jsx) and [this page about JSX gotchas](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/v15.4.0-rc.3/docs/docs/02.3-jsx-gotcha

title: Jsx Fragments (react)
description: Enforces the shorthand or standard form for React Fragments.

title: Jsx Handler Names (react)
description: Ensures that any component or prop methods used to handle events are correctly prefixed.

title: Jsx Max Depth (react)
description: Enforces a maximum depth for nested JSX elements and fragments.

title: Jsx Pascal Case (react)
description: Enforce PascalCase for user-defined JSX components.

title: Jsx Props No Spreading (react)
description: Disallow JSX prop spreading.

title: No Redundant Should Component Update (react)
description:
Disallow usage of `shouldComponentUpdate` when extending `React.PureComponent`.
Note that usage of `PureComponent` is [not recommended in modern React](https://react.dev/reference/react/PureComponent).

title: No Set State (react)
description: Disallow the usage of `this.setState` in React components.

title: Prefer Es6 Class (react)
description:
React offers you two ways to create traditional components: using the `create-react-class` package or the newer ES2015 class system.
Note that function components are preferred over class components in modern React, and it is especially discouraged to use `createReactClass` in modern React.

title: Self Closing Comp (react)
description: Detects components without children which can be self-closed to avoid unnecessary extra closing tags.

title: State In Constructor (react)
description:
Enforces the state initialization style to be either in a constructor or with a class property.
This rule is not relevant for function components, and so can potentially be disabled for modern React codebases.

title: Adjacent Overload Signatures (typescript)
description: Require that function overload signatures be consecutive.

title: Array Type (typescript)
description: Require consistently using either `T[]` or `Array<T>` for arrays.

title: Ban Tslint Comment (typescript)
description: This rule disallows `tslint:<rule-flag>` comments.

title: Class Literal Property Style (typescript)
description: Enforces a consistent style for exposing literal values on classes.

title: Consistent Generic Constructors (typescript)
description:
When constructing a generic class, you can specify the type arguments on either the left-hand side (as a type annotation) or the right-hand side (as part of the constructor call).
This rule enforces consistency in the way generic constructors are used.

title: Consistent Indexed Object Style (typescript)
Consistent Type Assertions (typescript)
description: Enforce consistent usage of TypeScript type assertions.

title: Consistent Type Definitions (typescript)
description: Enforce type definitions to consistently use either `interface` or `type`.

title: Consistent Type Exports (typescript)
description: Enforce using `export type` for exports that are only used as types.

title: Consistent Type Imports (typescript)
description:
Enforce consistent usage of type imports by adding or removing the `type` keyword from imports.
The `fixStyle` option controls where newly added `type` keywords are placed when this rule auto-fixes imports. It does not enforce the placement of `type` keywords that are already present in the code. To enforce consistent placement, use `import/consistent-type-specifier-style`.

title: Dot Notation (typescript)
description: Enforce dot notation whenever property access can be written safely as `obj.prop`.

title: Method Signature Style (typescript)
description: Enforce using a particular method signature syntax.

title: No Empty Interface (typescript)
description: Disallow the declaration of empty interfaces.

title: No Inferrable Types (typescript)
description: Disallow explicit type declarations for variables or parameters initialized to a number, string, or boolean.

title: No Unnecessary Qualifier (typescript)
description: Disallow namespace qualifiers when the referenced name is already in scope.

title: Parameter Properties (typescript)
description: Requires or disallows parameter properties in class constructors.

title: Prefer Find (typescript)
description: Prefer `.find(...)` over `.filter(...)[0]` for retrieving a single element.

title: Prefer For Of (typescript)
description: Enforces the use of a `for...of` loop instead of a `for` loop with simple iteration.

title: Prefer Function Type (typescript)
description: Enforce using function types instead of interfaces with call signatures.

title: Prefer Readonly (typescript)
description: Require class members that are never reassigned to be marked `readonly`.

title: Prefer Reduce Type Parameter (typescript)
description: This rule prefers using a type parameter for the accumulator in `Array#reduce()` instead of casting.

title: Prefer Regexp Exec (typescript)
description: Prefer `RegExp#exec()` over `String#match()` when extracting a regex match.

title: Prefer Return This Type (typescript)
description: This rule enforces using `this` types for return types when possible.

title: Prefer String Starts Ends With (typescript)
description: Prefer `startsWith` and `endsWith` over manual string boundary checks.

title: Unified Signatures (typescript)
description: Disallow overload signatures that can be unified into one.

title: Catch Error Name (unicorn)
description: This rule enforces consistent and descriptive naming for error variables in `catch` statements, preventing the use of vague names like `badName` or `_` when the error is used.

title: Consistent Date Clone (unicorn)
description: The Date constructor can clone a `Date` object directly when passed as an argument, making timestamp conversion unnecessary. This rule enforces the use of the direct `Date` cloning instead of using `.getTime()` for conversion.

title: Consistent Existence Index Check (unicorn)
description: Enforce consistent style for element existence checks with `indexOf()`, `lastIndexOf()`, `findIndex()`, and `findLastIndex()`. This ensures that comparisons are performed in a standard and clear way.

title: Consistent Template Literal Escape (unicorn)
description: Enforce consistent style for escaping `${` in template literals.

title: Custom Error Definition (unicorn)
description: Enforces the only valid way of Error subclassing. It works with any super class that ends in Error.

title: Empty Brace Spaces (unicorn)
description: Removes the extra spaces or new line characters inside a pair of braces that does not contain additional code. This ensures that braces are clean and do not contain unnecessary spaces or newlines.

title: Error Message (unicorn)
description: Enforces providing a `message` when creating built-in `Error` objects to improve readability and debugging.

title: Explicit Timer Delay (unicorn)
description: Enforce or disallow explicit `delay` argument for `setTimeout()` and `setInterval()`.

title: Filename Case (unicorn)
description:
Enforces a consistent case style for filenames to improve project organization and maintainability. By default, `kebab-case` is enforced, but other styles can be configured.
Files named `index.js`, `index.ts`, etc. are exempt from this rule as they cannot reliably be renamed to other casings (mainly just a problem with PascalCase).

title: Max Nested Calls (unicorn)
description:
Limit the depth of nested calls.
This rule counts calls and constructor calls passed into other calls or constructors. Fluent receiver chains and JSX wrappers are ignored.

title: No Array Method This Argument (unicorn)
description: Disallows the use of the `thisArg` parameter in array iteration methods such as `map`, `filter`, `some`, `every`, and similar.

title: No Await Expression Member (unicorn)
description: Disallows member access from `await` expressions.

title: No Console Spaces (unicorn)
description: Disallows leading/trailing space inside `console.log()` and similar methods.

title: No Nested Ternary (unicorn)
description:
Disallow deeply nested ternary expressions.
Nested ternary expressions that are only one level deep and wrapped in parentheses are allowed by this rule.

title: No Null (unicorn)
description: Disallow the use of the `null` literal, to encourage using `undefined` instead.

title: No Unreadable Array Destructuring (unicorn)
description: Disallows destructuring values from an array in ways that are difficult to read.

title: No Useless Collection Argument (unicorn)
description: Disallow useless values or fallbacks in `Set`, `Map`, `WeakSet`, or `WeakMap`.

title: No Zero Fractions (unicorn)
description: Prevents the use of zero fractions.

title: Number Literal Case (unicorn)
description: This rule enforces proper case for numeric literals.

title: Numeric Separators Style (unicorn)
description: Enforces a convention of grouping digits using numeric separators.

title: Prefer Array Index Of (unicorn)
description: Enforces using `indexOf` or `lastIndexOf` instead of `findIndex` or `findLastIndex` when the callback is a simple strict equality comparison.

title: Prefer Bigint Literals (unicorn)
description: Requires using BigInt literals (e.g. `123n`) instead of calling the `BigInt()` constructor with literal arguments such as numbers or numeric strings

title: Prefer Class Fields (unicorn)
description: Prefers class field declarations over `this` assignments in constructors for static values.

title: Prefer Classlist Toggle (unicorn)
description: Prefers the use of `element.classList.toggle(className, condition)` over conditional add/remove patterns.

title: Prefer Default Parameters (unicorn)
description:
Instead of reassigning a function parameter, default parameters should be used. The `foo = foo || 123` statement evaluates to `123` when `foo` is falsy, possibly leading to confusing behavior, whereas default parameters only apply when passed an `undefined` value. This rule only reports reassignments to literal values.
You should disable this rule if you want your functions to deal with `null` and other falsy values the same way as `undefined`. Default parameters are exclusively applied when `un

title: Prefer Dom Node Text Content (unicorn)
description: Enforces the use of `.textContent` over `.innerText` for DOM nodes.

title: Prefer Export From (unicorn)
description: When re-exporting from a module, it's unnecessary to import and then export. It can be done in a single export…from declaration. This rule encourages using direct re-export syntax (export ... from) instead of importing and then exporting. It helps reduce boilerplate code and keeps the module scope clean by avoiding unnecessary local bindings.

title: Prefer Global This (unicorn)
description:
Enforces the use of `globalThis` instead of environment‑specific global object aliases (`window`, `self`, or `global`).
Using the standard `globalThis` makes your code portable across browsers, Web Workers, Node.js, and future JavaScript runtimes.

title: Prefer Includes (unicorn)
description: Prefer `includes()` over `indexOf()` when checking for existence/non-existence. All built-ins have `.includes()` in addition to `.indexOf()`.

title: Prefer Keyboard Event Key (unicorn)
description:
Enforces the use of `KeyboardEvent#key` over `KeyboardEvent#keyCode`, which is deprecated.
The `.key` property is also more semantic and readable.

title: Prefer Logical Operator Over Ternary (unicorn)
description: This rule finds ternary expressions that can be simplified to a logical operator.

title: Prefer Modern Dom Apis (unicorn)
description:
Enforces the use of:
- `childNode.replaceWith(newNode)` over `parentNode.replaceChild(newNode, oldNode)`
- `referenceNode.before(newNode)` over `parentNode.insertBefore(newNode, referenceNode)`
- `referenceNode.before('text')` over `referenceNode.insertAdjacentText('beforebegin', 'text')`
- `referenceNode.before(newNode)` over `referenceNode.insertAdjacentElement('beforebegin', newNode)`

title: Prefer Negative Index (unicorn)
description: Prefer using a negative index over `.length - index` when possible.

title: Prefer Object From Entries (unicorn)
description: Encourages using `Object.fromEntries` when converting an array of key-value pairs into an object.

title: Prefer Optional Catch Binding (unicorn)
description: Prefers omitting the catch binding parameter if it is unused.

title: Prefer Reflect Apply (unicorn)
description: Disallows the use of `Function.prototype.apply()` and suggests using `Reflect.apply()` instead.

title: Prefer Response Static Json (unicorn)
description: Enforces the use of `Response.json()` over `new Response(JSON.stringify())`.

title: Prefer Spread (unicorn)
description: Enforces the use of the spread operator (`...`) over outdated patterns.

title: Prefer String Raw (unicorn)
description: Prefers use of `String.raw` to avoid escaping `\`.

title: Prefer String Trim Start End (unicorn)
description: `String#trimLeft()` and `String#trimRight()` are aliases of `String#trimStart()` and `String#trimEnd()`. This is to ensure consistency and use [direction](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/CSS/Building_blocks/Handling_different_text_directions)-independent wording.

title: Prefer Structured Clone (unicorn)
description: Prefer using `structuredClone` to create a deep clone.

title: Prefer Ternary (unicorn)
description: Prefers ternary expressions over simple `if`/`else` statements.

title: Relative Url Style (unicorn)
description: Enforce consistent relative URL style.

title: Require Array Join Separator (unicorn)
description: Enforce using the separator argument with `Array#join()`.

title: Require Module Attributes (unicorn)
description: This rule enforces a non-empty attribute list in `import`/`export` statements and `import()` expressions.

title: Switch Case Braces (unicorn)
description: Requires empty switch cases to omit braces, while non-empty cases must use braces. This reduces visual clutter for empty cases and enforces proper scoping for non-empty ones.

title: Switch Case Break Position (unicorn)
description: Enforce consistent `break`/`return`/`continue`/`throw` position in `case` clauses.

title: Text Encoding Identifier Case (unicorn)
description:
This rule enforces consistent casing for text encoding identifiers, specifically:
- `'utf8'` instead of `'UTF-8'` or `'utf-8'` (or `'utf-8'` if `withDash` is enabled)
- `'ascii'` instead of `'ASCII'`

title: Throw New Error (unicorn)
description: This rule makes sure you always use `new` when throwing an error.

title: Consistent Each For (vitest)
description: This rule enforces consistency in which method is used to create parameterized tests. This configuration affects different test function types (`test`, `it`, `describe`, `suite`).

title: Consistent Test Filename (vitest)
description: This rule triggers an error when a file is considered a test file, but its name does not match an expected filename format.

title: Consistent Test It (vitest)
description:
Vitest allows you to choose how you want to define your tests, using the `it` or the `test` keywords, with multiple permutations for each:
- it: `it`, `it.only`, `it.skip`, `it.concurrent`, `it.each`.
- test: `test`, `test.only`, `test.skip`, `test.concurrent`, `test.each`.

title: Consistent Vitest Vi (vitest)
description: This rule triggers an error when an unexpected Vitest accessor is used.

title: Max Expects (vitest)
description: This rule enforces a maximum number of `expect()` calls in a single test.

title: Max Nested Describe (vitest)
description: This rule enforces a maximum depth to nested `describe()` calls.

title: No Alias Methods (vitest)
description: Enforces Vitest's canonical matcher names instead of aliases.

title: No Duplicate Hooks (vitest)
description: Disallows duplicate hooks in describe blocks.

title: No Hooks (vitest)
description: Disallows Jest setup and teardown hooks, such as `beforeAll`.

title: No Identical Title (vitest)
description: This rule looks at the title of every test and test suite. It will report when two test suites or two test cases at the same level of a test suite have the same title.

title: No Import Node Test (vitest)
description: This rule warns when `node:test` is imported (usually accidentally). With `--fix`, it will replace the import with `vitest`.

title: No Importing Vitest Globals (vitest)
description: The rule disallows importing any Vitest global functions.

title: No Interpolation In Snapshots (vitest)
description: Prevents the use of string interpolations in snapshots.

title: No Large Snapshots (vitest)
description: Disallow large snapshots.

title: No Mocks Import (vitest)
description: This rule reports imports from a path containing a `__mocks__` component.

title: No Restricted Matchers (vitest)
description: Ban specific matchers & modifiers from being used, and can suggest alternatives.

title: No Restricted Vi Methods (vitest)
description: Restrict the use of specific `jest` and `vi` methods.

title: No Test Prefixes (vitest)
description: Require using `.only` and `.skip` over `f` and `x`.

title: No Test Return Statement (vitest)
description: Disallow explicitly returning from tests.

title: No Unneeded Async Expect Function (vitest)
description: Disallows unnecessary async function wrapper for expected promises.

title: Padding Around After All Blocks (vitest)
description: This rule enforces a line of padding before and after 1 or more `afterAll` statements.

title: Padding Around Test Blocks (vitest)
description: This rule enforces a line of padding before and after 1 or more `test`/`it` statements.

title: Prefer Called Exactly Once With (vitest)
description: It checks when a target is asserted with both `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` and `toHaveBeenCalledWith` instead of `toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith`.

title: Prefer Called Once (vitest)
description: Substitute `toBeCalledTimes(1)` and `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` with `toBeCalledOnce()` and `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` respectively.

title: Prefer Called Times (vitest)
description: This rule aims to enforce the use of `toBeCalledTimes(1)` or `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` over `toBeCalledOnce()` or `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()`.

title: Prefer Called With (vitest)
description: Suggest using `toBeCalledWith()` or `toHaveBeenCalledWith()`

title: Prefer Comparison Matcher (vitest)
description:
This rule checks for comparisons in tests that could be replaced with one of the following built-in comparison matchers:
- `toBeGreaterThan`
- `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`
- `toBeLessThan`
- `toBeLessThanOrEqual`

title: Prefer Describe Function Title (vitest)
description: When testing a specific function, this rule aims to enforce passing a named function to `describe()` instead of an equivalent hardcoded string.

title: Prefer Each (vitest)
description: This rule enforces using `each` rather than manual loops.

title: Prefer Equality Matcher (vitest)
description: Jest has built-in matchers for expecting equality, which allow for more readable tests and error messages if an expectation fails.

title: Prefer Expect Assertions (vitest)
description: Enforces that every test has either `expect.assertions(<number>)` or `expect.hasAssertions()` as its first expression.

title: Prefer Expect Resolves (vitest)
description: Prefer `await expect(...).resolves` over `expect(await ...)` when testing promises.

title: Prefer Expect Type Of (vitest)
description: Enforce using `toBeTypeOf` instead of `expect(typeof ...).toBe(...)`.

title: Prefer Hooks In Order (vitest)
description: Ensures that hooks are in the order that they are called in.

title: Prefer Hooks On Top (vitest)
description: While hooks can be setup anywhere in a test file, they are always called in a specific order, which means it can be confusing if they're intermixed with test cases.

title: Prefer Import In Mock (vitest)
description: This rule enforces using a dynamic `import()` in `vi.mock()` or `vi.doMock()`, which improves type information and IntelliSense for the mocked module.

title: Prefer Importing Vitest Globals (vitest)
description: Enforces explicit imports from 'vitest' instead of using Vitest globals.

title: Prefer Lowercase Title (vitest)
description: Enforce `it`, `test`, `describe`, and `bench` to have descriptions that begin with a lowercase letter. This provides more readable test failures.

title: Prefer Mock Promise Shorthand (vitest)
description: When working with mocks of functions that return promises, Jest provides some API sugar functions to reduce the amount of boilerplate you have to write. These methods should be preferred when possible.

title: Prefer Mock Return Shorthand (vitest)
description: When working with mocks of functions that return simple values, Jest provides some API sugar functions to reduce the amount of boilerplate you have to write.

title: Prefer Spy On (vitest)
description:
When mocking a function by overwriting a property you have to manually restore the original implementation when cleaning up. When using `jest.spyOn()` Jest keeps track of changes, and they can be restored with `jest.restoreAllMocks()`, `mockFn.mockRestore()` or by setting `restoreMocks` to `true` in the Jest config.

title: Prefer Strict Boolean Matchers (vitest)
description: Enforce using `toBe(true)` and `toBe(false)` over matchers that coerce types to boolean.

title: Prefer Strict Equal (vitest)
description: This rule triggers a warning if `toEqual()` is used to assert equality.

title: Prefer To Be (vitest)
description: Recommends using `toBe` matcher for primitive literals and specific matchers for `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN`.

title: Prefer To Be Falsy (vitest)
description: This rule warns when `toBe(false)` is used with `expect` or `expectTypeOf`. With `--fix`, it will be replaced with `toBeFalsy()`.

title: Prefer To Be Object (vitest)
description: This rule enforces using `toBeObject()` to check if a value is of type `Object`.

title: Prefer To Be Truthy (vitest)
description: This rule warns when `toBe(true)` is used with `expect` or `expectTypeOf`. With `--fix`, it will be replaced with `toBeTruthy()`.

title: Prefer To Contain (vitest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toContain()` should be used upon asserting expectations on an array containing an object.

title: Prefer To Have Been Called Times (vitest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` should be used instead of directly checking the length of `mock.calls`.

title: Prefer To Have Length (vitest)
description: In order to have a better failure message, `toHaveLength()` should be used upon asserting expectations on objects length property.

title: Prefer Todo (vitest)
description: When test cases are empty then it is better to mark them as `test.todo` as it will be highlighted in the summary output.

title: Require Hook (vitest)
description:
This rule flags any expression that is either at the toplevel of a test file or directly within the body of a `describe`, except for the following:
- `import` statements
- `const` variables
- `let` declarations, and initializations to `null` or `undefined`
- Classes
- Types
- Calls to the standard Jest globals

title: Require Top Level Describe (vitest)
description: Requires test cases and hooks to be inside a top-level `describe` block.

title: Component Definition Name Casing (vue)
description: Enforce specific casing for component definition names.

title: Define Emits Declaration (vue)
description: Enforce consistent declaration style for `defineEmits` in Vue. This rule only works in `<script setup>` with `lang="ts"`.

title: Define Props Declaration (vue)
description: Enforce consistent declaration style for `defineProps` in Vue. This rule only works in `<script setup>` with `lang="ts"`.

title: Define Props Destructuring (vue)
description: This rule enforces a consistent style for handling Vue 3 Composition API props, allowing you to choose between requiring destructuring or prohibiting it.

title: Next Tick Style (vue)
description: Enforce Promise or callback style in `nextTick`.

title: Prop Name Casing (vue)
description: Enforce a specific casing (camelCase or snake_case) for Vue component prop names.

title: Require Default Prop (vue)
description: Requires default value to be set for props that are not marked as `required`.

title: Require Direct Export (vue)
description: This rule requires that the component object be directly exported.

title: Require Prop Types (vue)
description: This rule enforces that a props statement contains a type definition.

title: Require Typed Ref (vue)
description: Require `ref` and `shallowRef` functions to be strongly typed.

title: No Restricted Exports (eslint)
description:
This rule disallows specified names from being used as exported names.
By default, this rule doesn’t disallow any names. Only the names you specify in the configuration will be disallowed.

title: No Undef (eslint)
description:
Disallow the use of undeclared variables.
This rule can be disabled for TypeScript code, as the TypeScript compiler enforces this check.

title: No Unreachable Loop (eslint)
description: Disallow loops whose body allows only one iteration.

title: No Useless Assignment (eslint)
description: Flags assignments where the newly assigned value is never read afterward (a "dead store"). This helps catch wasted work or accidental mistakes.

title: Export (import)
description: Reports funny business with exports, like repeated exports of names or defaults.

title: Named (import)
description:
Verifies that all named imports are part of the set of named exports in the referenced module.
For `export`, verifies that all named exports exist in the referenced module.
Note: for packages, the plugin will find exported names from `jsnext:main` (deprecated) or `module`, if present in `package.json`. Redux's npm module includes this key, and thereby is lintable, for example.

title: No Return In Finally (promise)
description: Disallow return statements in a `finally()` callback of a promise.

title: Require Render Return (react)
description:
Require render methods in ES5 and ES2015 React components to return a value.
This rule is not relevant for function components, and so can potentially be disabled for modern React codebases.

title: No Unnecessary Condition (typescript)
description: Disallow conditions that are always truthy, always falsy, or always nullish based on TypeScript's type information.

title: Prefer Optional Chain (typescript)
description:
Enforce using concise optional chain expressions instead of chained logical AND operators, negated logical OR operators, or empty objects.
Note that this rule is in the nursery category while we ensure it is working correctly in as many edge-case scenarios as possible. The logic for this is complex and the autofix may cause logic changes in some edge-cases.

title: No Useless Iterator To Array (unicorn)
description: Disallow unnecessary `.toArray()` on iterators.
